C015-WIP12 APPEND -- F152 same-group pathfinder membership invalidation defect
===============================================================================

F152 / provisional KI#475 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVC/K-MOD PATH-CACHE DEFECT,
CURRENT SAS SAME-TURN SETTLER-ESCORT TRIGGER
GROUP MEMBERSHIP CAN CHANGE MOVEMENT LEGALITY WITHOUT INVALIDATING REUSABLE PATH DATA
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT.
- The reusable GroupPathFinder architecture and missing membership invalidation
  are already present in Base AdvCiv 1.14's K-Mod-derived pathfinder line.
- Current SAS supplies a deterministic same-turn trigger through its Settler
  city-escort attachment and a shipped equal-move restrictive escort (Chariot).
- Civ4CE/BtS uses the older executable FAStar pathfinder; this audit does not
  establish the same node-cache defect there, so ancestry is pinned no earlier
  than the AdvCiv/K-Mod-derived GroupPathFinder implementation.

Broken cache contract:
- CvSelectionGroup::generatePath uses the shared reusable GroupPathFinder and
  binds it through GroupPathFinder::setGroup(*this, flags, maxPath).
- setGroup resets when the CvSelectionGroup POINTER changes, or when relevant
  movement flags change. It does not detect a changed member list inside the
  same group object.
- CvSelectionGroup::addUnit and removeUnit mutate m_units without calling
  invalidateGroupPaths. CvUnit::joinGroup reaches exactly those operations.
- invalidateGroupPaths is currently used when the emptied group is killed, not
  whenever a surviving group's membership changes.
- GroupStepMetric::canReuseInitialPathData itself warns that its reuse key does
  not catch every significant change. In the current implementation it accepts
  reuse when recalculated initialMoves equals the cached start-node moves.
- Membership can change much more than that key: feature/terrain legality,
  all-terrain movement, movement costs, combat/danger inputs and group strength,
  while leaving the minimum current moves unchanged.

Why stale nodes alter later results:
- KmodPathFinder caches initialized nodes across generatePath calls with the same
  start. resetNodes is deliberately skipped when the cached start data is judged
  reusable.
- processChild calls GroupStepMetric::canStepThrough ONLY for an UNINITIALIZED
  child node. Already-initialized children are reused without rerunning current
  group movement legality.
- Conversely, a newly examined impossible intermediate tile is permanently set
  PATHNODE_CLOSED, with the source comment explicitly assuming that it can never
  become enterable on a later generatePath call (except as destination).
- That assumption is valid only while the movement-relevant group state remains
  equivalent. Changing members of the same group violates it.
- The destination fast path is even clearer: if the destination node was already
  initialized, generatePath immediately reuses it as m_pEndNode; an already-found
  cached path is not reconstructed under the new member set before success is
  reported.

Deterministic current-SAS same-turn reproduction:
1. Use an AI UNIT_SETTLER standing in one of its own cities, unescorted and with
   its full 2 moves. Give the player at least one currently considered city site
   reachable only by crossing a neutral/foreign Forest or Jungle intermediate
   tile.
2. Keep at least three healthy local defenders so the shipped default
   SAS_AI_SETTLER_ATTACH_CITY_ESCORT_MIN_HEALTHY_CITY_DEFENDERS_LEFT = 2 permits
   one defender to be reassigned. Make the best eligible local escort a healthy
   UNIT_CHARIOT with its full moves.
3. Current UNIT_SETTLER has iMoves=2 and no feature-impassability. During
   AI_settleMove, before AI_found is called, the city-site scan invokes
       generatePath(kSite, MOVE_NO_ENEMY_TERRITORY, true)
   on the Settler-only group. The neutral Forest/Jungle route is legal and its
   nodes/destination are cached in the shared finder.
4. AI_settleMove then calls AI_found with the SAME movement flags.
5. At the start of AI_found, current SAS calls SAS_tryAttachCityEscortToSettler
   while the Settler is unescorted in its own city. The helper chooses a healthy
   defender by base combat strength and joins it directly to pSettlerGroup.
6. Current UNIT_CHARIOT is a valid canDefend escort candidate, has iMoves=2, and
   is feature-impassable in Forest and Jungle outside its own team's territory.
   UNITAI_SETTLE's group-first value remains above UNITAI_ATTACK, so the Settler
   also remains group head after attachment.
7. Because both fully ready units have 2 moves, the group's minimum moves after
   attachment still equals the cached Settler-only start-node moves. Same group
   pointer + same start + same relevant flags + same initialMoves therefore pass
   the existing reuse checks despite the new movement restriction.
8. AI_found immediately pathfinds the same city-site set again. The cached route
   or destination reached while the group was Settler-only can be reported as
   reachable even though the newly attached Chariot makes the required neutral
   Forest/Jungle step illegal.

Concrete gameplay consequence:
- AI_found trusts the stale successful generatePath result when selecting
  pBestFoundPlot / pBestPlot and then returns true after pushing its
  MISSION_MOVE_TO for the cached end-turn plot.
- AI mission commands execute immediately. CvSelectionGroup::groupPathTo uses
  the separately cleared alternate finder, now with the actual Settler+Chariot
  composition. If the stale selected step/target requires the impassable feature
  and has no legal alternate route, this fresh execution path correctly fails.
- continueMission_bulk marks the MOVE_TO done on that no-path result and removes
  the mission. But AI_found has already returned true to AI_settleMove, whose
  caller returns for the turn. Thus the cache mismatch can deterministically
  produce a selected Settler target/move that immediately evaporates and wastes
  that AI update/turn instead of evaluating the post-escort group coherently.
- Even where a fresh alternate route exists, the main-finder result can still
  supply stale path turns/end-turn choice and therefore distort site comparison
  before the execution finder repairs the route. The root is incorrect reusable
  path state, not merely the final mission failure shape.

Reverse-direction risk:
- The same cache hole also supports restrictive -> permissive membership changes:
  an intermediate node closed under a departed restrictive member can remain
  PATHNODE_CLOSED after the remaining group becomes able to traverse it.
- A previous attempted Catapult/Swordsman AI_guardCity reproduction used this
  direction, but it is deliberately NOT used as the current proof: current SAS
  now forbids Catapults from UNITAI_COLLATERAL and their ATTACK_CITY ordering no
  longer guarantees the restrictive non-head unit is the one ejected.
- The shipped Settler+Chariot attachment above is simpler, current-tree exact and
  immediate; no inter-group scheduling assumption is required.

Ancestry/control comparison:
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same GroupStepMetric reuse warning, same setGroup
  pointer/flag reset architecture, and no addUnit/removeUnit membership
  invalidation. The structural defect is therefore inherited by SAS.
- Current SAS's same-turn trigger is custom: AI_settleMove first pathfinds, then
  AI_found may attach a defender directly to that still-live Settler group and
  pathfind again.
- Civ4CE/BtS instead routes CvSelectionGroup::generatePath through the executable
  FAStar interface and an explicit bReuse parameter. Without visibility into an
  equivalent cached-node contract, do not backdate F152 to Firaxis.

Relation to other file-015 roots:
- Distinct from F149 / KI#472 amphibious execution: F149 consumes a transport
  landing mission after treating a pushed but individually illegal cargo move as
  a successful landing attempt.
- Distinct from F151 / KI#474 action cache: F151 collapses same-UnitType units
  despite per-unit upgrade price; F152 is reusable map-path state surviving a
  changed member set.
- The current Settler escort hook belongs to KI#179, but KI#179's intended
  behavior (attach a spare defender before exposed founding) is valid. It merely
  exposes the inherited path-cache contract because attachment happens between
  two reusable path searches.
- No current reviewed Known-Issues collision for provisional KI#475 found.

Repair direction:
- Invalidate shared pathfinder state whenever membership of a surviving
  CvSelectionGroup actually changes, rather than trying to enumerate every
  movement/combat property in GroupStepMetric::canReuseInitialPathData.
- addUnit/removeUnit (or the single lower ownership boundary reached by both)
  are the natural correctness boundary. Invalidation should occur only when the
  membership mutation really happens, and must cover both shared pathfinders if
  either can still be bound to the group.
- Review clearUnits/full teardown separately: kill already invalidates before the
  group object is deleted, but normal surviving-group add/remove is the missing
  case.
- A narrower Settler-only reset would hide this reproduction but leave all other
  regroup/split/merge callers vulnerable to the same stale-node assumption.

C015-WIP13 APPEND -- F153 cross-transport cargo group wrongly boarded as a whole
===============================================================================

SOURCE RECONCILIATION AT THIS CONTINUATION
-----------------------------------------
- Current uploaded AdvCiv-SAS light source is practical 6272 / HEAD
  202064cbf9db8a00ce0df4c0f36f8bc9027271cf. CvSelectionGroup.cpp remains
  4,722 lines and is unchanged by the unrelated reviewed worktree edits.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and Civ4CE are used locally for ancestry/control comparison.
- C015-WIP12 remains an exact byte prefix of this checkpoint. No repository
  source file is modified by the audit.


F153 / provisional KI#476 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVC.075 CARGO-CYCLING DEFECT
SUPPORTED K-MOD CROSS-TRANSPORT CARGO GROUPS RECEIVE ONE TRANSPORT GROUP'S
ACTIVITY_BOARDED STATE AS A WHOLE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT.
- Introduced by Base AdvCiv's advc.075 boarded/cargo-cycling convenience layer,
  interacting with a grouping state explicitly supported by K-Mod.
- Current SAS inherits the same helper logic essentially unchanged.
- Civ4CE/BtS has no ACTIVITY_BOARDED / resetBoarded / handleBoarded layer, so
  this audit does not backdate the defect to Firaxis.

Broken ownership/state contract:
- CvSelectionGroup::startMission calls resetBoarded() for a HUMAN SEA group
  before dispatching the mission switch. This is not limited to ship movement;
  MISSION_SKIP and other accepted ship orders pass through the same call.
- resetBoarded() calls getLandCargoGroups(), then changes every returned
  selection group's activity from ACTIVITY_AWAKE to ACTIVITY_BOARDED.
- getLandCargoGroups() correctly filters individual cargo units by carrier:
      pUnit->getTransportUnit()->getGroup() == this
  but then returns pUnit->getGroup(), i.e. the cargo unit's entire LAND
  CvSelectionGroup.
- That selection group is not required to consist solely of cargo carried by
  this SEA selection group.
- CvUnit::canJoinGroup only requires compatible owner, plot and domain (plus the
  force-separate guard). It has no same-transport or same-transport-group rule.
  Human GAMEMESSAGE_JOIN_GROUP reaches CvUnit::joinGroup directly, so land cargo
  aboard different carriers on the same plot can legitimately share one group.
- Activity is selection-group-wide. ACTIVITY_BOARDED is a waiting activity;
  isCycleGroup excludes waiting groups from normal automatic unit cycling.
  resetBoarded therefore applies ship A's "cargo should become inactive" state
  to unrelated cargo on ship B whenever those cargo units share a group.

Minimal deterministic human reproduction -- no ship movement required:
1. Put two separate human sea transport selection groups, ship A and ship B, on
   the same coastal water tile. Give each at least one land cargo unit.
2. Manually select/group cargo A and cargo B. Same owner, same plot and both
   DOMAIN_LAND satisfy canJoinGroup, so they form one AWAKE cargo group despite
   being carried by different transport groups.
3. Select only ship A and give it MISSION_SKIP (or any other legal order that
   reaches startMission). Ship B receives no order and need not move.
4. startMission on ship A calls resetBoarded before the mission switch.
5. getLandCargoGroups sees cargo A because cargo A's carrier belongs to ship A's
   group, but pushes cargo A's SHARED selection-group pointer.
6. resetBoarded sets that whole shared group to ACTIVITY_BOARDED. Cargo B is now
   BOARDED solely because ship A received an order, although cargo B's own
   carrier ship B remained untouched.
7. With normal unit cycling enabled, the shared cargo group is a waiting group
   and is excluded from ordinary cycling. If ship B stays put, there is no
   generic per-turn BOARDED wake that restores cargo B; advc.075 normally wakes
   boarded cargo through the carrier-side movement/arrival handling. The player
   can therefore silently lose the expected prompt for otherwise idle cargo on
   an unrelated stationary transport. Manual selection still remains possible.

Why this contradicts the feature's own intent:
- Base AdvCiv history for advc.075 says: "When a ship is given an order, units
  in cargo that are awaiting orders are treated as if they had just boarded the
  ship" and become inactive until that ship reaches another destination.
- The current implementation identifies an affected cargo MEMBER correctly by
  its actual carrier, but stores the resulting inactivity on that member's whole
  selection group. Cargo on a different ship is therefore swept into the state
  transition even though that ship was not given the order.

K-Mod cross-transport grouping is a supported state, not a fabricated API case:
- K-Mod's changelog explicitly says cargo units stay grouped when their
  transports move unless the transports carrying parts of the group are
  separated, and its amphibious AI groups cargo before landing.
- CvUnit::setXY contains corresponding live logic: after a transport moves its
  cargo, it detects cargo groups that include units not transported by this
  transport group and separates the left-behind members.
- That separation deliberately preserves the cargo group's old activity when it
  is not ACTIVITY_MISSION. Thus, if resetBoarded has already assigned the shared
  group ACTIVITY_BOARDED, cargo on another carrier can be split off and retain
  the wrongly inherited BOARDED state. This corroborates the ownership mismatch
  but is not required by the simpler MISSION_SKIP reproduction above.

Ancestry:
- K-Mod commit/changelog 58faf9a7 (2011-12-16) explicitly supports cargo staying
  grouped across transport movement until the relevant transports separate.
- Base AdvCiv introduced ACTIVITY_BOARDED on 2019-02-18 to wake cargo when a ship
  reaches land, then advc.075 on 2019-02-20 added reset-on-ship-order / ship-first
  cycling behavior. A 2019-03-16 refinement groups awoken cargo for convenience.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same resetBoarded/getLandCargoGroups contract.
- Civ4CE has no ACTIVITY_BOARDED or corresponding helpers. F153 is therefore an
  AdvCiv-layer defect exposed by a legitimate K-Mod grouping invariant.

Relation to earlier cargo observations:
- During this audit getLandCargoGroups was already noted to append duplicate
  CvSelectionGroup pointers when multiple cargo members belong to the same group.
  That is at most redundant traversal here; it is NOT the F153 root.
- Deduplicating those pointers would still set the same mixed-carrier cargo
  group to ACTIVITY_BOARDED once, leaving cargo B wrongly affected.
- The root is scope: a per-carrier/per-transport-group event is represented by a
  state transition on a cargo selection group that may span other carriers.

Repair direction:
- Preserve advc.075's intended convenience, but apply "boarded because THIS sea
  group got an order" only to cargo actually carried by that sea group.
- When an affected cargo unit belongs to a selection group containing members
  carried by other transport groups, partition/split the relevant cargo before
  applying ACTIVITY_BOARDED, or otherwise represent the state at the correct
  carrier/member scope.
- Review handleBoarded symmetrically: it also consumes cargo-group pointers and
  can wake/merge a whole mixed-carrier group based on one sea group's arrival.
  A repair should avoid transferring wake/merge effects to unrelated carriers.
- Do not treat pointer deduplication as the fix; it may be a small cleanup but
  does not restore the ownership contract.


NEIGHBOR CONTROL -- INITIAL MIXED PLUNDER ADMISSION IS NOT A NEW ROOT
---------------------------------------------------------------------
A mixed group such as a Destroyer that can plunder plus a Transport that cannot
can pass group MISSION_PLUNDER because canDoMission is any-member, after which
startMission puts the whole selection group in ACTIVITY_PLUNDER while only the
eligible unit gets unit-local m_bBlockading state.

This looks superficially similar to F143/F144, but current evidence does NOT
justify a new F154 or a broadening of those roots:
- the ineligible escort does not later cancel the eligible unit's blockade;
- it has no stale unit-local blockading state to reconcile;
- keeping a manually grouped escort waiting with the blockading group is a
  plausible and internally consistent group-activity semantic.
F143 remains specifically the Sea Patrol member that later wakes/cancels the
valid patrol; F144 remains the destructive divergence after a formerly valid
blockader loses legality and group wake clears still-valid blockaders.

C015-WIP14 APPEND -- F154 BtS cross-transport cargo automation scope leak
===============================================================================

F154 / provisional KI#477 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED FIRAXIS BTS DEFECT
STOPPING AUTOMATION ON ONE TRANSPORT GROUP CANCELS AUTOMATION FOR CARGO CARRIED
BY ANOTHER TRANSPORT GROUP WHEN THEIR LAND CARGO SHARES A SELECTION GROUP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT.
- Present already in supplied Civ4CE/BtS; absent from the supplied Civ4 and
  Warlords CvSelectionGroup::setAutomateType implementations.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS inherit the BtS cargo-cancellation block.
- Distinct from F153 / KI#476: F153 is AdvCiv's later ACTIVITY_BOARDED/cycling
  layer. F154 predates that feature and corrupts AutomateTypes state instead.

Broken ownership/state contract:
- CvSelectionGroup::setAutomateType(NO_AUTOMATE) contains the BtS convenience:
      // If canceling automation, cancel on cargo as well.
- It scans units on the transport group's plot and correctly identifies an
  affected cargo MEMBER by checking:
      pCargoUnit->getTransportUnit()->getGroup() == this
- It then applies both NO_AUTOMATE and ACTIVITY_AWAKE to:
      pCargoUnit->getGroup()
  i.e. the member's entire LAND selection group.
- CvUnit::canJoinGroup does not require cargo members to have the same carrier
  or even carriers in the same sea selection group. Same owner, plot and domain
  are sufficient (plus the force-separate guard).
- Human grouping reaches CvUnit::joinGroup through the normal
  GAMEMESSAGE_JOIN_GROUP path. Thus land cargo carried by separate transport
  groups on the same plot can legitimately share one selection group.
- The per-transport event "automation on sea group A was canceled" therefore
  mutates automation state belonging to cargo on sea group B as well.

Current-SAS deterministic human reproduction:
1. Put two separate human transport selection groups, ship A and ship B, on the
   same city/coastal plot. Load one land combat cargo unit on each.
2. Group cargo A and cargo B through normal human selection/grouping. Their
   different carriers do not prevent canJoinGroup.
3. Set the shared cargo group to AUTOMATE_EXPLORE. Current CvUnit::canAutomate
   explicitly permits DOMAIN_LAND combat units to Explore even while cargo; it
   has no isCargo exclusion. Loading has already finishMoves()'d the units, so
   assigning automation need not make them act immediately.
4. Automate ship A (e.g. Explore) so its sea group has a non-NO automate type.
   Ship B remains a separate transport group and need receive no matching order.
5. Issue COMMAND_STOP_AUTOMATION (or another path that genuinely transitions
   ship A from an automate type to NO_AUTOMATE) on ship A.
6. ship A's setAutomateType(NO_AUTOMATE) finds cargo A by its actual carrier,
   then calls setAutomateType(NO_AUTOMATE) on cargo A's SHARED land group.
7. Cargo B, whose carrier ship B was untouched, has its AUTOMATE_EXPLORE state
   silently canceled solely because it was grouped with cargo A.
8. This is persistent gameplay state, not presentation only: unloading wakes a
   cargo group through CvUnit::setTransportUnit(NULL) but does NOT clear or
   restore its automate type. Without F154, cargo B could retain its automation
   for later use after unloading; after ship A's cancellation it cannot.

Why ordinary human reachability is supported:
- CvGame::selectUnit / selectGroup and CvDLLWidgetData::doCreateGroup ultimately
  issue GAMEMESSAGE_JOIN_GROUP; CvNetJoinGroup::Execute calls CvUnit::joinGroup.
- canJoinGroup has no carrier-affinity test. The required mixed-carrier land
  group therefore does not rely on a private or debug-only API state.
- K-Mod additionally treats cross-transport cargo grouping as meaningful and
  contains explicit separation logic when transport groups carrying different
  members later move apart. That strengthens present-day reachability, although
  the underlying F154 cancellation block already exists in Firaxis BtS.

Ancestry/control comparison:
- Supplied Civ4CE/BtS CvSelectionGroup::setAutomateType (around lines 3643-3674)
  contains the same "if canceling automation, cancel on cargo as well" loop and
  the same pCargoUnit->getGroup() state mutation.
- Supplied Warlords and original Civ4 setAutomateType implementations merely set
  the automate type, clear the mission queue and wake the group; they have no
  cargo-propagation loop.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 carries the BtS loop essentially unchanged. Current SAS does
  too. F154 therefore originates in Firaxis BtS, not K-Mod/AdvCiv/SAS.
- BtS movement tended to split cargo groups more aggressively when transports
  moved; K-Mod later preserves such grouping when possible. That can change how
  often the mixed-carrier state survives movement, but does not remove the
  stationary/manual-group reproduction or the original scope mismatch.

Relation to F153 / KI#476:
- Both defects expose the same underlying data-model fact: a land cargo
  CvSelectionGroup is not owned by one carrier/sea group.
- They remain separate roots because different code, state and ancestry are
  involved. F153 applies AdvCiv ACTIVITY_BOARDED wake/cycle semantics from one
  ship order/arrival; F154 applies Firaxis BtS automation cancellation from one
  sea group's automate transition.
- A common repair helper may be sensible, but fixing only resetBoarded /
  handleBoarded would leave F154 untouched, and fixing only setAutomateType would
  leave F153 untouched.

Repair direction:
- Propagate NO_AUTOMATE/AWAKE only to cargo actually carried by the sea selection
  group whose automation is being canceled.
- If such cargo shares a land selection group with members carried by other sea
  groups, partition/split at the carrier/transport-group boundary before making
  a group-wide state transition, or otherwise apply state at an appropriately
  scoped representation.
- Reuse the same carrier-partition invariant considered for F153 if practical;
  pointer deduplication alone is again insufficient.
- Preserve the intended BtS convenience that canceling a transport's automation
  also cancels automation of ITS cargo; the defect is only the spillover to
  another transport group's cargo.

C015-WIP15 APPEND -- F155 live groupMove traversal invalidated by move side effects
===============================================================================

F155 / provisional KI#478 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED WARLORDS/BTS DEFECT;
EXPLICITLY FIXED BY K-MOD 1.46 BUT STILL PRESENT IN ADVCIV/SAS DIVERGENT GROUPMOVE
POTENTIAL USE-AFTER-FREE / CTD WHEN GROUPMOVE PREFETCHES A FUTURE LIVE LIST NODE
AND MOVING THE CURRENT UNIT INDIRECTLY REGROUPS THAT FUTURE UNIT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT, crash-class rather than merely tactical/UI behavior.
- Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 traverse the live CvSelectionGroup unit list
  inside groupMove while CvUnit::move can run reentrant game-state code that
  changes membership of that same group.
- The concrete conquest/culture-bump mechanism is already present in supplied
  Warlords and BtS, so the reproduction is inherited Firaxis behavior at least
  from Warlords onward.
- K-Mod commit 1129c1e740 (2016-09-28), included in the K-Mod 1.46 history,
  explicitly fixed this exact class by making groupMove use a copied list of
  units rather than the live list. Current AdvCiv/SAS groupMove still uses live
  traversal because this function has a deliberately divergent advc.001 path.

Current-SAS vulnerable traversal:
- CvSelectionGroup::groupMove performs two no-city-capture stages and traverses
  the group through:
      FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN(pUnit, *this)
- LinkedListTraversal.h implements the VAR macro by obtaining the CURRENT unit
  and then prefetching the NEXT CLLNode before entering the loop body:
      pUnit = ::getUnit(node->m_data)
      node = CLinkList<IDInfo>::static_next(node)
      // body may now call pUnit->move(...)
- This safely permits deleting pUnit's CURRENT node in the body. It does NOT
  protect the already-prefetched NEXT node from being deleted indirectly.
- AdvCiv's own advc.003s manual documents exactly that limitation: after
  nextUnitNode has been called, the saved next node and the unit represented by
  that node must not be deleted. Otherwise the saved CLLNode pointer dangles.

Concrete current-SAS reentrant invalidation chain:
1. groupMove begins iterating selection group G and resolves current unit A.
2. The traversal macro prefetches the linked-list node for next unit B before
   executing A's loop body.
3. A can move into and capture an enemy city through pUnit->move(*pPlot, true).
4. CvUnit::move -> CvUnit::setXY processes the city conquest and calls
   CvPlayer::acquireCity(...).
5. The conquest branch of acquireCity calls:
      GC.getMap().verifyUnitValidPlot();
   after the culture/ownership transition.
6. CvMap::verifyUnitValidPlot visits plots. CvPlot::verifyUnitValidPlot can bump
   units that are no longer legal on their plots because borders/territory have
   just changed. Current K-Mod-derived code records the affected selection
   groups and then calls regroupSeparatedUnits() on them.
7. If still-unmoved future member B of G is one of the units displaced by that
   conquest/culture update, CvSelectionGroup::regroupSeparatedUnits removes B
   from G with CvUnit::joinGroup(...), thereby deleting B's old linked-list node.
8. But groupMove's traversal has already saved a pointer to exactly that node as
   its NEXT node. When the for-loop condition resumes, it dereferences the
   dangling CLLNode pointer to obtain node->m_data.
9. Result is undefined behavior: depending on allocator/memory reuse this can
   skip/corrupt traversal or produce a use-after-free crash-to-desktop.

Why this is not merely a theoretical mutation warning:
- K-Mod's retained commit history contains commit 1129c1e740 with subject:
      Fixed potential pointer invalidation in CvSelectionGroup::groupMove
  and explains the mechanism directly:
      The selection group can be messed up when units move. eg. If a city is
      captured, the change in culture could bump the remaining units.
  Its stated repair is to use a copied list of units rather than the live list.
- K-Mod 1.46 changelog separately records:
      Fixed potential crash in CvSelectionGroup::groupMove
- This independently identifies the same function, same state change and same
  failure class that current static tracing reaches.
- AdvCiv's own linked-list refactor documentation further says the mutable
  prefetch idiom remains unsafe when a different, already-prefetched node is
  deleted as a side effect. The current groupMove call chain supplies exactly
  that prohibited mutation.

Ancestry/control comparison:
- Supplied original Civ4 groupMove already uses the same Firaxis idiom:
      pLoopUnit = ::getUnit(pUnitNode->m_data);
      pUnitNode = nextUnitNode(pUnitNode);
      pLoopUnit->move(...);
  However, supplied original Civ4 acquireCity does not show the conquest-time
  global verifyUnitValidPlot call used by this deterministic reproduction.
  F155 is therefore not backdated to Vanilla solely from loop shape.
- Supplied Warlords keeps the same live traversal AND its conquest branch calls
  GC.getMapINLINE().verifyUnitValidPlot(). CvPlot::verifyUnitValidPlot can move
  invalid units with jumpToNearestValidPlot. Thus the relevant reentrant
  membership-change family is present by Warlords.
- Supplied BtS keeps the same live traversal and conquest-time map verification.
- K-Mod later diagnosed the pointer invalidation explicitly and fixed groupMove
  by traversing a copied list.
- Base AdvCiv history says K-Mod 1.46 changes were broadly merged, including a
  rare CTD fix, but Base AdvCiv 1.14/current SAS groupMove still contains the
  older live traversal. The source itself explains why this function diverged:
  its advc.001 Gunship/no-city-capture staging comment says K-Mod 1.45 rewrote
  groupMove but merging that rewrite would also require reconciling the Gunship
  city-capture fix. Whatever other k146 code was merged, the copied-list safety
  property is absent from this current function.

Current implementation makes the old hazard especially explicit:
- Warlords/BtS used a hand-written while loop that prefetched nextUnitNode before
  calling move. AdvCiv refactored that shape into FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN.
- The macro improves readability and makes deletion of the CURRENT node safe,
  but it intentionally retains the same next-node-prefetch contract; it cannot
  make deletion of a FUTURE prefetched node safe.
- Therefore the modern macro is not a repair for the K-Mod 1.46 bug.

Repair direction:
- Restore the K-Mod 1.46 safety invariant: do not iterate the live selection-
  group CLinkList across calls to CvUnit::move that can reenter membership-
  mutating code.
- Snapshot the units/identities to be considered before movement and iterate
  that snapshot. Because reentrant effects can move, regroup or potentially
  destroy future members, an IDInfo-style snapshot with a fresh ::getUnit lookup
  and current-group/current-validity check before acting is safer than assuming
  raw pointers necessarily remain usable.
- Preserve current AdvCiv/SAS two-stage no-city-capture ordering and advc.153
  behind-group behavior while changing only the iteration ownership/lifetime
  contract.
- Do not rely on FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN as the fix: its documented guarantee covers
  deletion of the current node, not deletion of the prefetched next node by a
  nested side effect.

Distinctness:
- F155 is independent of F152 pathfinder invalidation. F152 concerns stale path
  cache state after legitimate group membership changes; F155 concerns unsafe
  linked-list traversal while the membership change occurs reentrantly.
- It is also independent of mission/cargo group-state roots F143-F154. Fixing
  any of those does not make groupMove traversal lifetime-safe.

C015-WIP16 APPEND -- F156 outer updateTimers traversal invalidated by combat regroup
===============================================================================

F156 / provisional KI#479 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED BASE ADVCIV INTERACTION DEFECT
POTENTIAL USE-AFTER-FREE / CTD WHEN UPDATETIMERS PREFETCHES A FUTURE UNIT NODE,
UPDATECOMBAT ADVANCES THE WINNER, AND ADVC.153 SPLITS THAT FUTURE UNIT FROM GROUP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT, crash-class linked-list lifetime failure.
- Distinct from F155 / KI#478. F155 is the live traversal INSIDE groupMove while
  CvUnit::move can reentrantly remove a future node. F156 is the caller one
  level above: updateTimers keeps its own prefetched future node across
  CvUnit::updateCombat, and a perfectly normal groupMove membership change can
  delete that node before updateTimers resumes.
- Supplied stock BtS has the same next-node prefetch in updateTimers but breaks
  immediately after updating one fighting unit, so the prefetched node is never
  consumed after updateCombat. K-Mod deliberately disabled that break so that
  several queued combats in one selection group can be updated.
- Current deterministic reproduction additionally uses Base AdvCiv change
  advc.153: on a normal MANUAL HUMAN combat advance, non-attacking members are
  deliberately split from the attacker's original group rather than advancing
  with it. The proven current root is therefore classified conservatively as a
  Base AdvCiv inherited interaction defect, rather than backdating the exact
  failure to K-Mod from architecture alone.

Vulnerable outer traversal:
- Current CvSelectionGroup::updateTimers uses:
      FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN(pUnit, *this)
      {
          if (pUnit->isInCombat())
          {
              ...
              pUnit->updateCombat();
              bCombat = true;
              //break; // disabled by K-Mod.
          }
      }
- LinkedListTraversal.h's mutable traversal obtains the current unit and
  PREFETCHES the next CLLNode before entering the body. As documented for F155,
  this supports deletion of the CURRENT node but not deletion of the already-
  saved NEXT node by a nested side effect.
- Because K-Mod removed the old break, updateTimers will attempt to resume the
  loop through that saved next-node pointer after updateCombat returns.

Deterministic current-SAS reproduction:
1. Create a manually controlled human land selection group G with at least two
   ordinary city-capturing combat units. Arrange attacker A as the group/best
   attacker and B immediately after it in G's unit list. A and B need not have
   different unit types; choosing A clearly stronger avoids attacker-selection
   ambiguity.
2. With Quick Combat off, order G to attack an adjacent visible enemy unit on a
   non-city plot that has no other visible enemy defender. Stack Attack can be
   OFF; this is the simplest control because groupAttack starts A's visible
   combat and then stops issuing further attacks.
3. The visible fight remains active across timer ticks. On the finishing tick,
   CvSelectionGroup::updateTimers resolves current unit A while its traversal
   has already prefetched B's live group-list node.
4. CvUnit::updateCombat clears A/defender combat state, kills the defeated final
   defender and computes bAdvance. With no visible enemy defenders remaining it
   executes:
       getGroup()->groupMove(pPlot, true, bAdvance ? this : NULL, true);
5. For a victorious ordinary attacker that can advance, groupMove first moves A
   to the target. Choose an ordinary non-city target so no conquest/culture
   invalidation from F155 is required for this reproduction.
6. Current groupMove's advc.153 state is:
       bool const bAIControl = isAIControlled();
       bool const bGroupAdvance = (!bCombat || bAIControl);
   For a manually controlled human group, isAIControlled() is false; with
   bCombat=true, bGroupAdvance is therefore false.
7. In stage 0, ordinary B is consequently taken through the left-behind branch
   and pUnit->joinGroup(NULL, true) (or joins an already-created behind group).
   CvUnit::joinGroup removes B from original G; CvSelectionGroup::removeUnit ->
   deleteUnitNode -> CLinkList::deleteNode physically deletes B's OLD node.
8. Control returns from groupMove and then updateCombat to the OUTER
   updateTimers loop. Its traversal variable still points at exactly that freed
   old B node. With the K-Mod break disabled, loop continuation dereferences the
   dangling CLLNode to obtain its IDInfo.
9. Result is undefined behavior / use-after-free: allocator state can turn it
   into stale traversal, memory corruption or a crash-to-desktop.

Why the normal combat path satisfies groupMove's safety assertions:
- updateCombat reaches the advancement code only after the finishing combat
  timer has elapsed and it has called setAttackPlot(NULL), setCombatUnit(NULL)
  and pDefender->setCombatUnit(NULL).
- Thus the simple two-unit reproduction no longer has an active combat object
  keeping G busy when groupMove executes; its FAssert(!isBusy()) does not rule
  out this path.
- The dangerous removal is also not an exotic nested ownership event. It is the
  intended advc.153 group-splitting branch itself.

Ancestry/control comparison:
- Supplied Civ4CE/BtS updateTimers manually performs the same structural
  prefetch:
      pLoopUnit = ::getUnit(pUnitNode->m_data);
      pUnitNode = nextUnitNode(pUnitNode);
      ... pLoopUnit->updateCombat();
  but then immediately executes:
      break;
  Therefore stock BtS does not return to the prefetched node through this
  sequence.
- Current source retains a K-Mod comment explaining why that break was disabled:
  groupAttack was changed so multiple units in one group can be queued for
  combat, and updating only the first can otherwise cause an infinite loop.
  Restoring the BtS break is therefore not a correctness repair.
- Base AdvCiv history records commit 9ffb0d869861f50784f03f968fc8acd6a471460f
  (2021-01-28), "Merge branch split-groups-after-missions," as change advc.153.
  Current groupMove explicitly tags bGroupAdvance and the human left-behind
  partition branches with advc.153.
- I have not established from the supplied historical material that pre-advc.153
  K-Mod itself had an equally deterministic future-node deletion during this
  exact updateTimers call chain. The defensible provenance is therefore:
  BtS prefetch + K-Mod no-break are prerequisites, while current proven
  membership deletion is supplied by Base AdvCiv advc.153; SAS inherits it.

Why F155's repair is insufficient:
- F155 can be fixed perfectly by snapshotting the iteration INSIDE groupMove.
  groupMove must still legitimately remove B from G to implement advc.153.
- F156's dangling node was saved by updateTimers BEFORE entering updateCombat /
  groupMove. No internal groupMove iterator repair can revoke that outer saved
  pointer.
- Both traversal boundaries therefore need their own lifetime-safe strategy.

Repair direction:
- Preserve K-Mod's ability to update multiple queued combats; do not simply
  restore the stock-BtS break.
- Do not hold live m_units CLLNode pointers across updateCombat or
  updateAirCombat, because those calls can cause group membership changes.
- Snapshot unit identities before the traversal, then fresh-lookup each unit
  before updating it. Skip an identity if the unit no longer exists or no
  longer belongs to this CvSelectionGroup. This makes ownership explicit and
  also tolerates other nested combat-side membership/death effects.
- A copied-ID traversal is preferable to raw unit pointers because combat can
  destroy units as well as regroup them.
- Re-test queued same-group combats after the repair so the original K-Mod
  anti-infinite-loop purpose remains intact.

Negative controls examined while establishing F156:
- The MISSION_GOLDEN_AGE unit loop initially looked similar because
  killGoldenAgeUnits can consume several Great People. Those calls use
  CvUnit::kill(true), i.e. startDelayedDeath; the group-list nodes are not
  physically removed until later doDelayedDeath -> kill(false). It therefore
  does not reproduce this future-node invalidation during startMission.
- MISSION_AIRLIFT physically removes the acting unit from its old selection
  group because airlift -> setXY uses bGroup=false. That removes the CURRENT
  node, which the mutable iterator permits. removeUnit also clears the old
  mission queue, but current startMission checks
      getNumUnits() == 0 || headMissionQueueNode() == NULL
  after each action and breaks before a next iteration can dereference the
  cleared queue. No separate current-tree crash root was promoted there.

POST-F156 MUTATION / LIFETIME CLOSURE CONTROLS
----------------------------------------------
The remaining mutable-selection-group traversals were challenged specifically
for the lifetime pattern behind F155 and F156: the traversal macro prefetches a
live next CLLNode before entering the body, so deletion of the CURRENT node is
supported, while reentrant deletion of a FUTURE prefetched node is unsafe.
Several superficially dangerous sites close as negative controls:

1. CvSelectionGroup::doTurn
   - CvUnit::doTurn does not perform immediate kill(false), joinGroup, setXY or
     transport regrouping in the reviewed current implementation.
   - Unit death arising from turn processing is delayed and physically removed
     later through doDelayedDeath.
   - The saved pHeadUnit used by the surrounding turn-boundary logic therefore
     is not invalidated by a normal member's doTurn call in this path.
   - No F157 established.

2. CvSelectionGroup::doDelayedDeath
   - CvUnit::doDelayedDeath -> kill(false) removes the CURRENT unit-list node;
     that is the exact mutation the mutable traversal macro is designed to
     tolerate.
   - kill(false) recursively kills cargo before removing the carrier, so a
     same-group future cargo node would have been dangerous in principle.
     Current shipped SAS data closes that route concretely: every cargo-capable
     unit is DOMAIN_SEA, carrying DOMAIN_LAND or DOMAIN_AIR cargo, while
     CvUnit::canJoinGroup requires the selection group to have the same domain.
     Thus a transport and its carried units cannot occupy the same selection
     group whose future node is being traversed here.
   - No F157 established.

3. startMission action loop
   - MISSION_FOUND, religion/corporation spread, Great Person consumption and
     related consuming actions use delayed death during this loop; they do not
     physically delete a future selection-group node before loop continuation.
   - MISSION_GOLDEN_AGE was rechecked because killGoldenAgeUnits can consume
     several Great People. The unit kills are likewise delayed, matching the
     WIP16 negative control.
   - MISSION_AIRLIFT can physically move/ungroup the acting unit through setXY,
     but that is deletion of the CURRENT iteration node. Its old mission queue
     can also be cleared; startMission rechecks group emptiness/head mission and
     breaks before another action iteration can consume invalid queue state.
   - MISSION_PARADROP chooses the acting unit afresh through the mission helper;
     the earlier mutable pass only collects immobile units. No retained future
     group-list node crosses the paradrop setXY call.
   - No F157 established.

4. continueMission post-action split
   - The apCanMove vector is formed only under canAnyMove() && !canAllMove(), so
     apCanMove[0] is not an empty-vector access.
   - Members are subsequently regrouped from the saved unit pointers; no
     reviewed operation in that small split sequence kills an unprocessed unit
     as a side effect. This remains a valid raw-pointer use in the current
     shipped path rather than another linked-list-prefetch root.
   - No F157 established.

5. CvSelectionGroup::groupBuild
   - CvUnit::build may consume a build unit when the BuildInfo isKill flag is
     set, but it calls kill(true): delayed death. The live traversal therefore
     does not lose a future CLLNode during the build loop.
   - The later "stop other workers" pass traverses the plot, not this group's
     list, and deletes a MISSION QUEUE node from another group; it does not
     remove the iterated plot unit from that plot list.
   - No F157 established.

6. CvSelectionGroup::setTransportUnit
   - Loading explicitly expects setTransportUnit to ungroup the CURRENT unit;
     the loop breaks immediately after each successful load and restarts from
     the group's new head. This avoids consuming the prefetched next node.
   - Unloading clears the transport relation but current CvUnit::setTransportUnit
     does not ungroup the unloaded unit, so the unloading traversal remains
     structurally stable.
   - No F157 established.

7. CvSelectionGroup::unloadAll
   - Each transport's CvUnit::unloadAll first snapshots its cargo into a
     std::vector<CvUnit*> and only then clears transport links. Cargo units are
     cross-domain members of other selection groups; the outer selection-group
     traversal over the sea carriers does not delete a future carrier node.
   - No F157 established.

8. mergeIntoGroup / splitGroup / regroupSeparatedUnits
   - mergeIntoGroup removes the CURRENT member through joinGroup; if changing a
     UnitAI can regroup that current unit, it breaks and restarts deliberately.
   - splitGroup's mutable pass likewise joins only its CURRENT pLoopUnit to the
     split group. Mutable traversal's current-node deletion contract covers it.
   - regroupSeparatedUnits also moves only its CURRENT pLoopUnit. The retained
     head unit is deliberately left at the head plot and is not one of the
     members being removed in that loop.
   - No future-prefetched-node deletion comparable to F155/F156 was established.

9. setActivityType / NotifyEntity / airCircle / setBlockading
   - The group-level mutable loops call graphics/entity notification or update
     unit-local blockade accounting. Reviewed CvUnit implementations do not
     regroup, move or synchronously destroy selection-group members.
   - No F157 established.

10. Mission-queue ownership helpers
    - clearMissionQueue deactivates the current head mission before clearing the
      queue. deactivateHeadMission changes activity/timer state but does not
      recursively activate a replacement mission.
    - deleteMissionQueueNode deliberately leaves next-head activation to its
      caller; this avoids an immediate nested startMission while a caller still
      owns a live queue-node pointer.
    - continueMission copies MissionData before mutation-capable movement/combat
      work and explicitly refreshes headMissionQueueNode after groupAttack and
      after groupPathTo where the queue may have changed.
    - No new queue-node UAF root was established in this closure pass.


BOARDED / CARGO TAIL RECHECK
----------------------------
handleBoarded's duplicate cargo-group pointers remain a robustness/performance
quirk rather than a separate root:
- getLandCargoGroups can push the same selection-group pointer once per cargo
  unit carried by this sea group;
- after an earlier merge, the emptied old group object survives until delayed
  group death, and mergeIntoGroup on the already-target group is harmless
  because CvUnit::joinGroup immediately returns when the requested group is the
  unit's existing group;
- deduplicating these pointers would reduce redundant work but would NOT repair
  F153, whose defect is the cross-carrier scope of ACTIVITY_BOARDED itself.

The F154 automation sibling remains independently live for the same structural
reason: setAutomateType(NO_AUTOMATE) selects cargo by THIS transport group, then
writes automation/activity to the cargo UNIT'S WHOLE selection group. Fixing
only handleBoarded cannot fix that inherited BtS scope leak.

COMPLETED FILES: 14 / 169

C015-WIP18 APPEND -- F157 Firaxis Python queue-data ownership contract
======================================================================

F157 / provisional KI#480 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED FIRAXIS VANILLA PYTHON API DEFECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Summary:
The Python-exposed selection-group API getMissionFromQueue advertises Boost.Python
`manage_new_object` ownership even though CySelectionGroup forwards a pointer to
MissionData stored inside CvSelectionGroup's live CLinkList mission node. A Python
caller therefore receives an owning wrapper for memory that was not allocated as a
standalone object. When the wrapper is released, Boost's owning-holder policy deletes
that interior pointer, creating invalid-free / heap-corruption / crash risk. The same
Firaxis pattern also exists in CyCity::getOrderFromQueue for OrderData, establishing a
systemic queue-data binding root rather than an isolated SAS wrapper typo.

Current selection-group chain:

    // CvSelectionGroup.cpp
    MissionData* CvSelectionGroup::getMissionFromQueue(int iIndex) const
    {
        CLLNode<MissionData>* pMissionNode = m_missionQueue.nodeNum(iIndex);
        if (pMissionNode != NULL)
            return &(pMissionNode->m_data);
        return NULL;
    }

    // CySelectionGroup.cpp
    MissionData* CySelectionGroup::getMissionFromQueue(int iIndex)
    {
        return m_pSelectionGroup ?
            m_pSelectionGroup->getMissionFromQueue(iIndex) : NULL;
    }

    // CySelectionGroupInterface.cpp
    .def("getMissionFromQueue", &CySelectionGroup::getMissionFromQueue,
         python::return_value_policy<python::manage_new_object>(), ...)

The pointer returned to Python is therefore `&pMissionNode->m_data`: storage owned by
the CLinkList node, not by a `new MissionData` expression.

Why `manage_new_object` is not a harmless annotation:
- Boost.Python's manage_new_object policy routes pointer returns through an owning
  holder (`make_owning_holder`). The holder constructs an owning smart pointer from
  the returned raw pointer.
- Destruction of that Python-owned holder consequently performs deletion of the
  returned C++ pointer.
- That policy is correct for nearby wrappers such as CySelectionGroup::getHeadUnit,
  where the Cy wrapper actually executes `new CyUnit(...)` before returning.
- It is false for getMissionFromQueue, which forwards internal queue storage without
  allocating a new MissionData object.
- Queue mutation creates a second lifetime problem even before Python destruction:
  clearing/deleting that mission node invalidates the borrowed interior pointer while
  Python may still retain its wrapper.

Systemic Firaxis sibling:

    // CvCity.cpp
    OrderData* CvCity::getOrderFromQueue(int iIndex) const
    {
        CLLNode<OrderData>* pOrderNode = m_orderQueue.nodeNum(iIndex);
        if (pOrderNode != NULL)
            return &pOrderNode->m_data;
        return NULL;
    }

    // CyCity.cpp
    OrderData* CyCity::getOrderFromQueue(int iIndex)
    {
        return m_pCity ? m_pCity->getOrderFromQueue(iIndex) : NULL;
    }

    // CyCityInterface1.cpp
    .def("getOrderFromQueue", &CyCity::getOrderFromQueue,
         python::return_value_policy<python::manage_new_object>(), ...)

Thus the MissionData defect is not best explained as a K-Mod/AdvCiv/SAS regression;
Firaxis used the same ownership pattern for both exposed linked-list data structs.

Reachability / severity qualification:
- No current shipped SAS Assets/Python or PrivateMaps Python source calls
  getMissionFromQueue or getOrderFromQueue. Current UI code instead uses scalar-safe
  helpers such as getMissionType/getMissionData1/getMissionData2.
- Therefore this is NOT being promoted as a normal current-gameplay CTD reproduction.
  It is a dormant but real public-Python-API memory-ownership defect: a Python mod,
  event script, console command or future SAS code using the advertised API can trigger
  the invalid ownership contract directly.
- The bundled Python API documentation exposes both methods as returning MissionData /
  OrderData objects, so treating them as unsupported private internals would be wrong.

Minimal deterministic API reproduction shape:
1. Obtain a CySelectionGroup with at least one queued mission.
2. In Python, call `m = group.getMissionFromQueue(0)` and retain or release the result.
3. The binding constructs an owning Python holder around the address of the queue
   node's embedded MissionData.
4. When that owning wrapper is destroyed, its ownership policy attempts to delete the
   non-standalone pointer. Alternatively, clear the mission queue while retaining `m`;
   the Python object now refers to storage whose containing CLinkList node is gone.
5. Either path violates C++ object ownership/lifetime and can manifest as heap
   corruption or a crash; exact allocator timing need not be deterministic for the
   ownership bug itself to be deterministic.

Ancestry:
- Supplied Civ4CE Vanilla, Warlords and BtS all contain the same
  `return &(pMissionNode->m_data)` implementation and the same
  `return_value_policy<manage_new_object>` Python binding.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both unchanged, and current SAS retains them.
- F157 therefore originates in Firaxis Vanilla Civ4, not K-Mod, AdvCiv or SAS.

Repair direction:
- Keep the public Python behavior value-like and make the ownership policy truthful.
  In CySelectionGroup::getMissionFromQueue, obtain the internal MissionData pointer and
  return `new MissionData(*pMissionData)` when non-null. Then the existing
  manage_new_object policy correctly owns an independent heap object whose lifetime is
  unrelated to later mission-queue mutation.
- Apply the same repair to CyCity::getOrderFromQueue:
  return `new OrderData(*pOrderData)` for a valid queue entry.
- This is preferable to switching the binding to reference_existing_object: a borrowed
  reference would remain vulnerable to queue-node deletion and would expose writable
  Python fields directly onto live DLL queue state.
- The existing scalar mission getters remain useful and require no ownership change.
- Because this root spans CvSelectionGroup plus its Cy wrapper and has a proven CvCity
  sibling, implementation/review should search for any other `manage_new_object`
  bindings that forward pointers into container-owned POD storage before declaring the
  pattern globally closed.

Relation to earlier file-015 roots:
- F157 is independent of F155/F156. Those are C++ live-CLLNode traversal UAFs during
  nested group mutation; F157 is a cross-language ownership error at the Python ABI.
- It is independent of F151's action cache and all mission semantic roots F143-F150.
- A copied MissionData Python result also avoids stale queue-node lifetime by design;
  it does not alter mission execution or queue semantics inside CvSelectionGroup.

F158 / provisional KI#481 -- inherited AdvCiv isRemovableFeature current-research regression
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::isRemovableFeature incorrectly handles a feature-removing Build whose
normal build prerequisite and feature-removal prerequisite are different technologies.
After first testing whether the team already has both technologies, its fallback for
"CurrentResearch should be good enough" requires one player's single current research
to equal BOTH eTech1 and eTech2 simultaneously:

    if (kMember.getCurrentResearch() == eTech1 &&
        kMember.getCurrentResearch() == eTech2)
        return true;

For distinct prerequisites this can never succeed. The intended state -- one
prerequisite already known and the other being researched -- is therefore classified
as not removable even though the feature is about to become removable.

SHIPPED REPRODUCTION
Current BuildInfos supplies ordinary distinct-tech cases. For example, BUILD_FARM has
TECH_AGRICULTURE as its normal build prerequisite while Forest removal requires
TECH_MASONRY and Jungle removal requires TECH_METAL_CASTING. A team that already knows
Agriculture and is currently researching Masonry therefore fails the fallback for a
Forest Farm: currentResearch cannot simultaneously be Agriculture and Masonry.
Mine and other feature-removing build paths provide the same shape.

CONSEQUENCE
isRemovableFeature feeds the central city-site plot evaluation and the longer-horizon
evaluateWorkablePlot path. During the affected research turn(s), removable Forest /
Jungle can be treated as persistent or unavailable for improvement, changing feature
yield/health handling, improvement potential and found-value comparisons. This is a
scoring correctness regression, not merely a diagnostic mismatch.

ANCESTRY
The pre-refactor AdvCiv AI_foundValue logic used the correct independent condition for
each prerequisite: each tech could be either already known OR the player's current
research. AdvCiv commit

    078fc9bd7c7962bdd944073c372ffd2e5853b16e
    2019-12-15 -- "Move AI_foundValue computation into a new class"

split the logic into AIFoundValue::isRemovableFeature and introduced the impossible
same-current-research conjunction. Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it and current SAS inherits
it unchanged.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Test the two prerequisites independently. Conceptually, each prerequisite should pass
when NO_TECH, already held by the team, or currently researched by the relevant team
member. Do not require one current-research slot to equal two distinct technologies.
Keep team/member semantics consistent with the old known-good implementation.


F159 / provisional KI#482 -- inherited AdvCiv regression makes K-Mod other-island starting badness branch unreachable
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::adjustToStartingSurroundings currently wraps the nearby-plot evaluation
in:

    if ((p.isWater() || p.isArea(kArea)) && it.currPlotDist() <= iRange)

but later, inside that already-filtered block, retains K-Mod's intended distinction:

    if (p.isWater() || p.isArea(kArea))
        iR += iTempValue;
    else if (iTempValue >= 13)
        iGreaterBadTile++; // add at least 1 badness point for other islands.

For a land plot on another area, the outer condition has already rejected the plot.
The inner "other islands" else branch can therefore never execute.

INTENDED K-MOD CONTRACT
K-Mod commit

    51e5ee601626cd188f6beb21a0c0ea65de0bd471
    2015-01-24 -- "Land on other islands is now counted as \"bad\" for starting locations."

explicitly commented out the old outer same-area gate. Its diff also moved the yield
addition behind an inner area test: nearby other-island land should NOT contribute its
yields to the capital, because the capital cannot work it, but sufficiently good land
on that inaccessible island SHOULD increase the bad-tile count because it consumes
nearby geographic space without helping the starting city.

REGRESSION ANCESTRY
AdvCiv's 2017 initial import continuation

    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c
    2017-04-16 -- "Initial commit (cont.)"

restored the old outer same-area condition while retaining K-Mod's inner other-island
branch and comment. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS still have this contradictory
combination.

CONSEQUENCE
Starting-location surroundings can undercount inaccessible nearby land on a different
island/area. Such plots neither add usable yields nor the K-Mod badness point they were
specifically meant to add, so starts near tight coast/island boundaries can be rated
better than the intended K-Mod heuristic.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Restore K-Mod's structure: let the distance-qualified nearby plot reach the scoring
body regardless of land area, add iTempValue only for water or same-area land, and use
the existing other-island branch to add badness for sufficiently valuable but
unworkable land.


F160 / provisional KI#483 -- inherited Warlords/BtS bonus-improvement scan ignores actual plot domain; water Oil can use land Well timing/yields
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
AIFoundValue::getBonusImprovement receives the actual CvPlot& p, but its Build /
Improvement scan never verifies that a candidate improvement can exist on that plot.
It checks bonus validity/trade, technology nearness, feature-removal technology and
Fort exclusion, but not water/land domain (nor a stronger plot-validity predicate).

CURRENT SAS DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
Oil has two connecting improvements in current XML:

* IMPROVEMENT_WELL: bWater=0; Oil trade improvement; +2 production, +3 commerce;
  BUILD_WELL requires TECH_COMBUSTION.
* IMPROVEMENT_OFFSHORE_PLATFORM: bWater=1; Oil trade improvement; matching current
  Oil improvement yield; its build requires the later TECH_MARINE_TECHNOLOGY.

Well appears before Offshore Platform in the Build/Improvement iteration. Oil itself is
revealed and city-trade enabled at Combustion. Therefore, for a WATER Oil plot after
Combustion but before Marine Technology, getBonusImprovement can select the land-only
Well, set bCanImprove/bCanImproveSoon from Well's tech path, and calculate Well as the
chosen bonus improvement even though a Well cannot be built on that water tile.

This is not caused by SAS's recent decision to continue scanning after an available
improvement. In current data Well and Offshore Platform have tied Oil improvement
yields, and Well is encountered first, so Base AdvCiv's old early-available shortcut
also lands on Well. The deeper defect is the missing plot/domain validity check.

CONSEQUENCE
The timing flags are materially wrong even though current Well and Offshore Oil yield
bonuses happen to tie. calculateSpecialYieldModifier sees the water Oil as currently
or soon improvable and avoids the intended delayed-improvement discount. The
longer-horizon evaluateWorkablePlot path likewise can skip its later-era devaluation
because bCanSoonImproveBonus was derived from the illegal Well path. This can overrate
water Oil before Offshore Platforms are technologically available.

The file itself contains a useful negative control: evaluateWorkablePlot later asks

    GC.getInfo(eBonus).getTechImprove(p.isWater())

when it needs eventual bonus-improvement timing. CvBonusInfo::getTechImprove(bool
bWater) is explicitly domain-aware, demonstrating that land and water Oil technology
paths are expected to differ.

ANCESTRY
The same shape is present in supplied Firaxis Warlords CvPlayerAI::AI_foundValue:
it loops all improvements and picks the first isImprovementBonusMakesValid(eBonus)
without checking the resource plot's domain. BtS retains it. Supplied Vanilla Civ4
does not contain this same eBonusImprovement found-value path, so the root is best
classified as inherited Warlords/BtS rather than Vanilla.

K-Mod strengthened the resource check (notably BonusTrade), and AdvCiv later refactored
it. AdvCiv commit

    891273d300ade2b2adc69bb9cc0a907c74e59267
    2019-12-21 -- "AI city placement tweaks"

added/used the actual plot parameter while fixing resource tech/yield details, but the
scan still did not acquire a domain/plot-legality test. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
therefore retain the Firaxis root.

REPAIR DIRECTION
At minimum reject improvement candidates whose water/land domain disagrees with p.
A stronger solution can use the existing SAS bonus-specific plot/domain helper or an
appropriate plot-validity predicate, provided it does not accidentally require current
technology when this routine intentionally predicts near-future improvements.

RELATED NON-FINDING / LATENT SIBLING
Current SAS calculateBonusConnectionEra performs a similar all-Build scan without plot
domain filtering, so water Oil can nominally inherit Well's earlier Industrial-era
connection path there too. However, the current connection-era adjustment only acts on
positive explicit health/happiness/building-effect non-yield value. Current Oil has
zero health and happiness and no positive counted building health/happiness effect, so
this sibling has no demonstrated shipped scoring consequence at present. It is kept as
a latent robustness concern rather than a separate root.


F161 / provisional KI#484 -- current SAS contested-future-BFC helper filters rival cities by the candidate site's unrelated area
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
SAS's isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC(CvPlot const& p) is asked whether the SPECIFIC bonus
plot p is threatened by a known rival future BFC. Its rival-city loop nevertheless
contains:

    if (!pCity->isArea(kArea))
        continue;

AIFoundValue::kArea is not p's area. It is permanently bound in the constructor to the
land area of the NEW candidate city site kPlot currently being evaluated. The helper is
called while scanning bonus plots around all EXISTING own cities. Candidate site and
existing bonus can therefore be on entirely different continents.

DETERMINISTIC CROSS-AREA REPRODUCTION
1. Existing own city A is on land area A. An unowned Maize lies in A's future BFC.
2. Known rival city R, also on area A, has that same Maize within CITY_PLOTS_RADIUS;
   the Maize is genuinely contested and ownership is not reliable.
3. Evaluate a new city candidate B on a different land area B containing another
   Maize (or otherwise causing the same bonus type to be scored).
4. isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC(Maize) finds A's Maize and calls
   isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC on that plot.
5. Rival R is skipped solely because R is not on candidate B's kArea.
6. The helper falsely reports the A-area Maize unopposed; the caller then treats Maize
   as already reliably covered.

CONSEQUENCE
This is more than the flat diversity nudge. In current evaluate(), a falsely
"already covered" bonus loses the configured
SAS_EVALUATE_UNOWNED_BONUS_EXTRA_VALUE (currently 250). The same helper is also used by
nonYieldBonusValue to initialize bSurplus; false surplus status zeroes the candidate
copy's explicit health/happiness and counted building-effect value. Overseas/colony
site comparisons can therefore be distorted based on a rival-city filter tied to an
unrelated candidate continent.

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
The helper was introduced in SAS commit

    6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da
    2026-07-11 -- "(Fixed/Improved) City-site bonus valuation used broad trade-style
    AI_bonusVal instead of settlement-specific long-term value and other related AI
    bonus settler valuation issues (KI#178)"

whose commit message explicitly says to avoid over-counting reliable future-BFC
coverage WHILE PRESERVING value for contested bonuses. The current area filter violates
that exact contract.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Do not filter rival cities by AIFoundValue::kArea here. The radius-2 test already
localizes the scan to cities that can actually threaten p. Replacing kArea with
p.getArea() is also unsafe for coastal resources: a water bonus' area differs from the
land area containing the coastal rival city that can claim it. Removing the unrelated
area filter is the straightforward correctness-first repair.


F162 / provisional KI#485 -- current SAS future-BFC coverage result is order-dependent because the first matching bonus returns immediately
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC asks an empire-wide existential question: is this
bonus type already owned or reliably covered by ANY existing city's future BFC?
However, once it encounters the first matching unowned/self-owned bonus plot, it does:

    return !isPlotInKnownRivalFutureBFC(*pLoopPlot);

A contested first copy therefore returns false immediately and prevents the search
from discovering a later safely claimable copy of the same bonus type.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. The player does not yet have an actually available Maize.
2. Existing city A has an unowned Maize in its future BFC, but that plot is also inside
   a known rival city's future BFC and is therefore contested.
3. Existing city B has another unowned Maize in its future BFC with no known rival
   future-BFC contest; this second copy is reliable long-term coverage.
4. If the A/contested occurrence is encountered first in city/BFC iteration,
   isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC returns false immediately and never examines B.
5. If the safe occurrence is encountered first, the same empire state returns true.

CONSEQUENCE
Found value depends on city/BFC iteration order rather than resource-coverage state.
The false result can add the +250 unowned-resource diversity value to another Maize and
can preserve long-term non-yield Maize value even though a separate safe existing-city
copy already satisfies the helper's intended definition of reliable coverage.

INTRODUCTION / INTENT
This is independent of F161 but originates in the same KI#178 helper introduced by
SAS commit 6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da. F161 asks the wrong rivals because
of unrelated area state; F162 stops searching after one contested occurrence even when
that individual contest test itself is correct.

REPAIR DIRECTION
A contested matching plot should mean "this occurrence does not establish reliable
coverage; keep searching", not "the whole empire has no reliable copy". Return true
when any safe qualifying copy is found; after exhausting all copies, return false.


F163 / provisional KI#486 -- current SAS future-BFC helper counts temporary trade imports as owned despite explicit opposite contract
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT
The first line of isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC is:

    if (kPlayer.getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus) > 0)
        return true;

But CvPlayer::getNumAvailableBonuses reads the capital plot group's bonus count, and
CvPlot::updatePlotGroupBonus explicitly ADDS getBonusImport at the capital. The DLL
also defines:

    getNumTradeableBonuses(eBonus) =
        getNumAvailableBonuses(eBonus) - getBonusImport(eBonus)

so imported bonuses are demonstrably included in getNumAvailableBonuses.

This directly contradicts the active CitySiteEvaluator comment, XML define comment,
Main Changes Guide and KI#147/KI#178 documentation, all of which say that trade imports
DO NOT count as owned here because they are temporary/non-permanent.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
1. The player owns no Wheat and has no existing-city future-BFC Wheat that would count
   as reliable coverage.
2. The player temporarily imports Wheat in a resource trade deal connected to its
   capital network.
3. getNumAvailableBonuses(Wheat) becomes positive because imports are included in the
   capital plot-group bonus count.
4. Evaluate a post-capital candidate containing Wheat.
5. isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC returns true immediately because of the import.

CONSEQUENCE
The candidate Wheat can lose the configured +250 unowned-bonus diversity value, and
nonYieldBonusValue can set bSurplus and suppress the new permanent copy's explicit
health/happiness/building-effect settlement value. A cancellable trade deal is thus
allowed to erase precisely the permanent-resource value the SAS feature was designed
to preserve.

INTRODUCTION / REGRESSION ANCESTRY
KI#147's original SAS implementation (commit 24cf2b8853..., practical 5929) did NOT use
getNumAvailableBonuses. It scanned the player's cities with AI_countNumBonuses, which
did not convert temporary imports into owned map copies.

KI#178 commit

    6341d3d556a7f580e3664b8631d52446c2c7c4da

replaced that local scan with isBonusOwnedOrClaimedByFutureBFC and introduced the
getNumAvailableBonuses early return while retaining the explicit "Trade imports do not
count" contract. F163 is therefore a current SAS regression introduced by KI#178, not
an inherited AdvCiv defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION
Use an owned/permanent resource test that excludes getBonusImport. At minimum, do not
use raw getNumAvailableBonuses as the ownership predicate when its imported component
is explicitly outside this feature's semantics. Preserve the helper's later
existing-city/future-BFC coverage logic for not-yet-connected owned/claimable copies.
