POST-WIP11 CLOSURE / ANCESTRY NOTES
------------------------------------
The remaining work continues to be closure-oriented rather than finding-oriented.
F209 remains unused.

1. AI_follow mutable-list crash lineage: CLOSED / REJECTED AS CURRENT BUG
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
The old AdvCiv crash lineage around AI_follow was rechecked against current SAS.
AdvCiv practical 1282/1287 added defensive assertions around mutation of the group
while iterating its linked list. The subsequent K-Mod 1.46 merge (AdvCiv practical
1288 / <k146>) replaced that fragile traversal with the durable pattern still present
in current SAS: snapshot original members as a std::vector<IDInfo>, reacquire each
unit by ID, verify that the unit still belongs to this group before acting, and reset
the path whenever a follower acts and may mutate group composition.

The historical crash mechanism is therefore not merely presumed absent; current SAS
contains the upstream structural fix written for it. No F209.

2. SAS WAR_ATTACK_ORDER diagnostics: NO SIMULATION / RNG SIDE EFFECT FOUND
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The logging-only attacker diagnostics were challenged under the invariant that
raising gWarLogLevel must not change simulation state or RNG sequence. The extra
computations traced through attack-odds math, AI_sacrificeValue,
AI_currEffectiveStr, collateral estimation, defender lookup and LFB relative-value
rating. No synchronization RNG draw or gameplay-state mutation was found in the
logging-only work. It can add CPU/log I/O cost but does not currently establish an
OOS or attacker-selection side effect. No F209.

3. Human equal-value attacker tie-break history: INTENTIONAL LATER ADVCIV FIX
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
An older AdvCiv version guarded the human AI_sacrificeValue tie-break with an
odds-threshold condition. This was not accidentally lost: AdvCiv practical 2505,
"Fix attacker selection in combat odds display," deliberately removed the threshold
so equal-value human candidates use the sacrifice-value tie-break consistently in
the combat-odds display/selection path. Current SAS matches that later intended
behavior. No F209.

4. Loaded cargo in collateral estimation: REJECTED AS SIBLING OF F208
---------------------------------------------------------------------
During F208 follow-up, K-Mod's estimateCollateralWeight was noticed to count
canDefend() units without excluding isCargo(). That is NOT the same defect as F208.
Actual CvUnit::collateralCombat also chooses collateral victims through canDefend()
without excluding loaded cargo; loaded combat cargo can therefore legitimately be
hurt by collateral even though CvPlot::getBestDefender explicitly excludes cargo
from primary-defender selection.

This sharpens F208's boundary: cargo is wrong when AdvCiv 2809 counts units that can
prevent immediate city capture, but the same cargo population can be relevant to
collateral valuation. No additional root.

5. Sea weighted-odds !hasCargo() exemption: REJECTED AS COARSE K-MOD HEURISTIC
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_getWeightedOdds applies its special sea-stack adjustment only when !hasCargo().
Because cargo can include aircraft/missiles as well as invasion troops, this was
explicitly challenged after F206 exposed a different dangerous hasCargo capability
proxy. Here, however, the branch is an acknowledged K-Mod naval-combat heuristic,
not a movement/war-legality gate; its factor can raise or lower the adjusted odds
based on group/defender counts. No defensible invariant or concrete wrong action was
established for carrier/missile cargo. Preserve as coarse tuning, not F209.


F207 / KI#530 STRENGTHENING — OWNER FILTER ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH
---------------------------------------------------------------
F207 was originally proved through a foreign/neutral unit sharing the bombard tile:
AdvCiv 2809 scans the whole plot, does not restrict iAttackers to the human owner, and
uses canMoveOrAttackInto(target) so a third-party unit can count merely through
peaceful Open Borders entry.

A deeper current-SAS check proves a same-owner false-attacker case too. Spy units are
DOMAIN_LAND, have zero ordinary combat strength and rival-territory/invisibility
semantics that let them coexist with enemy units and enter hostile territory through
the ordinary movement half of canMoveOrAttackInto. Therefore a human Spy on the
bombard tile can increment iAttackers against a defended enemy city despite having no
ability to remove the defender.

The root is consequently broader than a missing owner filter:

    AdvCiv 2809 uses destination-entry eligibility as a proxy for immediate assault
    capability.

REPAIR BOUNDARY UPDATE
----------------------
A same-owner filter remains necessary for the already-proved foreign-unit case, but
it is not sufficient. The attacker census must also require actual combat/assault
eligibility against the defended target rather than generic canMoveOrAttackInto.
F205 separately owns the zero-defender smart-bombard case, so the defended-target
predicate can be made attack-specific without conflating those roots.

This strengthening belongs to existing F207/KI#530. F209 remains unused.

1. SEPARATION HELPERS — MUTATION SAFETY RECONFIRMED
---------------------------------------------------
AI_separate, AI_separateNonAI, AI_separateAI, AI_separateImpassable and

pre-advances the linked-list node before executing the loop body specifically so
removing/joinGroup(NULL)-ing the current unit cannot invalidate traversal. This
matches the old manual K-Mod pattern that advanced nextUnitNode before detaching.
No helper-local invalidation defect found.

The remaining interesting state issue belongs to a caller rather than these helpers.

DEFERRED CROSS-FILE CANDIDATE — CvUnitAI::AI_assaultSeaMove stale bFull
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Do NOT assign a queue-041 F-number to this unless later evidence moves the fault into
CvSelectionGroupAI. Preserve it for the owning CvUnitAI.cpp audit/resweep.

A concrete caller-side stale-cache sequence exists:

- AI_assaultSeaMove caches bFull near entry as
      getGroup()->getCargo() > 0 && AI_getGroup()->AI_isFull().
- A legal group can contain one fully loaded UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA transport plus one
  empty UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA transport. The group-wide AI_isFull result is false because
  the empty hull is not full.
- When bAttack is already true, a later AI_separateEmptyTransports call can detach the
  empty hull. The surviving loaded group is now actually full, but this call site does
  not recompute the cached bFull value.
- If the immediately attempted AI_assaultSeaTransport action fails, later logic can
  reach the `else if (!bFull)` pickup branch using the stale false value.
- CvUnitAI::AI_pickup does not test free cargo capacity / isFull at entry; it only
  rejects units with nominal cargoSpace() <= 0 and can issue MISSIONAI_PICKUP wait or
  movement based on pickup counts. Therefore the now-full transport group can waste
  a decision/turn pursuing cargo it cannot load.

Related caller-side question to preserve for CvUnitAI.cpp: AI_assaultSeaMove may also
unloadAll() early under threat without immediately recomputing cached bEmpty/bFull if
its attack/retreat/safety attempts all fail. iCargo is calculated afterward, but the
booleans can remain stale. This related route is NOT yet proved; preserve it as a
follow-up candidate rather than a finding.

F209 / provisional KI#532 -- SAS low-power attacker ordering invokes ordinary
land/sea effective-strength logic during normal AI air strikes
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED SOURCE-LEVEL DEFECT; SAS REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY PRACTICAL 5286
SEVERITY/CONSEQUENCE: deterministic debug assertion during normal AI air strikes
with the optimization enabled; release builds currently degrade the air unit's
low-power rank to the helper minimum (1), which is normally behavior-neutral only
because ordinary AI aircraft groups are singletons.

ROOT
----
SAS practical 5286 added the optional bPreferLowPower parameter to
CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_getBestGroupAttacker and changed CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack
to pass `true` for the real AI attack loop. For non-human groups while
SAS_AI_GETBESTGROUPATTACKER_LOW_POWER_ATTACK_ORDER_OPTIMIZE is enabled, this causes
the selector to call:

    kLoopUnit.AI_currEffectiveStr(...)

for every eligible attacker.

AI_currEffectiveStr is the ordinary land/sea combat-strength estimator. It calls
CvUnit::currEffectiveStr -> currCombatStr/maxCombatStr, and maxCombatStr immediately
returns 0 when baseCombatStr() == 0. AI_currEffectiveStr then asserts:

    FAssertMsg(iCombatStrengthPercent > 0, "Non-combat unit?");

Current SAS aircraft use the separate air-combat strength family. Verified current
XML examples:

    UNIT_FIGHTER          DOMAIN_AIR  iCombat=0  iAirCombat=12
    UNIT_JET_FIGHTER      DOMAIN_AIR  iCombat=0  iAirCombat=24
    UNIT_BOMBER           DOMAIN_AIR  iCombat=0  iAirCombat=16
    UNIT_STEALTH_BOMBER   DOMAIN_AIR  iCombat=0  iAirCombat=20

The SAS define is currently enabled (`...LOW_POWER_ATTACK_ORDER_OPTIMIZE = 1`).

REACHABLE NORMAL-AI EXECUTION CHAIN
-----------------------------------
This is not limited to a debug UI helper and does not require a multi-air group:

1. CvUnitAI::AI_airStrike selects a real troop air-strike target. For an air strike
   rather than MISSION_AIRBOMB, it calls pushGroupMoveTo(target).
2. CvUnit::pushGroupMoveTo queues MISSION_MOVE_TO with the default movement flags.
   AI missions execute immediately.
3. CvSelectionGroup::continueMission_bulk sees a same-turn MISSION_MOVE_TO without
   MOVE_NO_ATTACK and first calls groupAttack(...).
4. groupAttack explicitly permits DOMAIN_AIR. Its initial attacker probe uses the
   inherited/default bPreferLowPower=false and can correctly identify the aircraft:
   canAirAttack() uses airBaseCombatStr(), and canMoveInto(target,true) delegates the
   air attack legality to canAirStrike(target).
5. Once a defender is confirmed, the real attack loop calls:

       AI_getBestGroupAttacker(..., !bMaxSurvival, bMaxSurvival, true)

   The final `true` is the SAS bPreferLowPower parameter introduced by practical 5286.
6. For an AI owner and the enabled define, bUseLowPower becomes true. Even a singleton
   Fighter/Bomber therefore enters the low-power branch and calls
   AI_currEffectiveStr, reaching the `"Non-combat unit?"` assertion because ordinary
   baseCombatStr is zero.

WHY THE EARLIER "DORMANT FOR SINGLETON AIR GROUPS" REJECTION WAS INCOMPLETE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
An earlier closure pass correctly observed that normal AI aircraft are effectively
singleton groups, so the *ordering choice* among multiple air attackers is normally
irrelevant. That did not make the new branch dormant: the selector still computes the
low-power key for the one aircraft before returning it. Therefore the wrong metric is
executed and its assertion is live even with exactly one unit.

This WIP explicitly supersedes that earlier rejection. The singleton observation
still bounds the current release-build gameplay impact; it does not remove the debug
contract failure.

RELEASE BUILD BEHAVIOR
----------------------
With assertions compiled out, ordinary effective strength starts at 0 for these air
units. The subsequent calculation remains at 0 in the normal aircraft case, and
AI_currEffectiveStr finally returns std::max(1, iR), collapsing the air attacker's
low-power strength rank to 1 rather than using iAirCombat.

For the currently normal singleton AI air group this does not change which unit is
selected, so the demonstrated present gameplay consequence is the debug assertion.
If AI multi-air groups are ever introduced/reached, the same defect would make their
low-power ordering semantically meaningless because ordinary aircraft strengths
collapse to the helper minimum instead of reflecting air combat strength.

ANCESTRY / ATTRIBUTION
----------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 does not have the low-power branch and does not pass the new
bPreferLowPower=true argument from groupAttack. SAS practical 5286 explicitly:

- added the bPreferLowPower parameter;
- enabled bUseLowPower for non-human groups under the SAS define;
- added AI_currEffectiveStr as the low-power primary key; and
- changed the real groupAttack loop to pass `true`.

Therefore this is a SAS regression rather than an inherited AdvCiv/K-Mod air-combat
assertion path.

F204/KI#527 remains a separate root. F204 is an inherited debug combat-help/Shift-hover
diagnostic that calls AI_compareStacks/AI_sumStrength for DOMAIN_AIR despite that
stack-strength routine explicitly excluding air. F209 is normal AI runtime introduced
by SAS 5286 and directly invokes AI_currEffectiveStr from the new low-power attacker
ordering. The callers, ownership and repair boundaries differ even though both expose
the broader fact that ordinary effective-strength helpers do not model air combat.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The minimal safe repair for the current feature is to disable the low-power ordering
path for DOMAIN_AIR (at group or candidate level) and fall back to inherited air
attacker selection. If low-power ordering for grouped aircraft is intentionally wanted
in the future, it needs an air-specific strength metric based on air combat strength;
feeding iAirCombat aircraft through ordinary currEffectiveStr is not valid.

This finding does NOT require changing the inherited assertion in AI_currEffectiveStr:
that assertion correctly catches callers feeding a non-ordinary-combat unit into a
helper whose contract assumes positive ordinary combat strength.

POST-WIP13 CLOSURE STATE
------------------------
The current-SAS delta pass is now even more informative: practical 5286 contains one
confirmed domain-contract regression (F209) despite the rest of its low-power ordering
arithmetic/tie logic surviving prior review. Continue checking the remaining public
function/caller matrix rather than assuming this finding closes queue 041 by itself.

F210 / provisional KI#533 -- inherited LFB attacker/odds path treats aircraft as
ordinary zero-strength combatants, corrupting grouped-air attacker selection
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED SOURCE-LEVEL DEFECT; INHERITED FROM BETTER BTS AI / K-MOD AND
PRESENT IN ADVCIV 1.14
SEVERITY/CONSEQUENCE: player-visible grouped-air attacker-order/help error; inherited
odds collapse also makes the intended <68% sacrifice threshold fire for aircraft
regardless of their real iAirCombat strength. Current AI aircraft are normally
singletons, which limits autonomous-AI ordering damage, but AdvCiv explicitly supports
human grouped-air stack execution and air-strike help through this selector.

ROOT
----
CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_getBestGroupAttacker explicitly accepts DOMAIN_AIR attackers:

    if (kLoopUnit.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_AIR)
        bCanAttack = kLoopUnit.canAirAttack();

but, unless SAS's newer low-power branch is active, it then sends those aircraft
through the inherited Lead-From-Behind path:

    kLoopUnit.LFBgetBetterAttacker(...)

LFBgetBetterAttacker -> CvUnit::LFBgetAttackerRank ->
pDefender->LFBgetDefenderOdds(pAttacker). LFBgetDefenderOdds decides whether it has a
usable attacker by evaluating ordinary combat strength:

    iAttStrength = pAttacker->currCombatStr();
    if (iAttStrength > 0)
        bUseAttacker = true;

Current aircraft have ordinary iCombat=0 and store their real strength in iAirCombat.
Thus Fighter/Jet Fighter/Bomber/Stealth Bomber all supply currCombatStr()==0 here.
LFB consequently takes its defender-only fallback and never incorporates the
attacker's air strength into the combat-odds ranking.

The sibling unit-level path has the same domain mistake. CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds is
explicitly air-aware in its old/fallback calculation:

    iOurStrength = (getDomainType() == DOMAIN_AIR ?
            airCurrCombatStr(NULL) : currCombatStr());

but the default LFB-enabled branch runs before that fallback and calls generic
calculateCombatOdds(*this, *pDefender). CombatOdds::setupCombatantsImpl initializes
its attacker with ordinary currCombatStr(), so an aircraft contributes zero ordinary
strength and the calculation immediately yields 0 attack odds. After personality
adjustment and the public clamp, ordinary air AI_attackOdds therefore collapses to the
minimum (typically 1%, or only the leader AttackOddsChange above that) instead of
reflecting iAirCombat.

ANCESTRY CROSS-CHECK
--------------------
Civ4CE/BtS's pre-LFB CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds reaches the explicit DOMAIN_AIR
`airCurrCombatStr` branch and therefore distinguishes aircraft by air strength.
K-Mod's Better BTS AI / Lead-From-Behind integration inserts the generic combat-odds
branch ahead of that air-aware calculation. AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same structure.
This is therefore inherited rather than introduced by SAS.

The current XML confirms the domain split rather than relying on a hypothetical unit:

    UNIT_FIGHTER          iCombat=0  iAirCombat=12  cost=140  interception=100
    UNIT_JET_FIGHTER      iCombat=0  iAirCombat=24  cost=170  interception=100
    UNIT_BOMBER           iCombat=0  iAirCombat=16
    UNIT_STEALTH_BOMBER   iCombat=0  iAirCombat=20

CONCRETE GROUPED-AIR CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------
AdvCiv explicitly supports grouped human aircraft. CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack has
advc.004c logic described as "Treat air combat like stack attack unless intercepted",
and CvGameTextMgr::getAirStrikePlotHelp asks the selected group's
AI_getBestGroupAttacker for the aircraft whose interception/help should be shown.
Therefore multi-air selection is a live supported caller, not merely a future AI
possibility.

Consider a full-health human group containing a Fighter and Jet Fighter attacking the
same weak ground defender. Both use UNITCOMBAT_AIR_FIGHTER, so the inherited LFB
fallback sees the same defender-side ordinary-strength context for them while seeing
neither 12 nor 24 air strength. More importantly, its returned iUnitOdds collapses to
about the minimum and therefore satisfies AdvCiv's explicit sacrifice gate:

    if (bSacrifice && iUnitOdds < 68)
        pBestUnit = AI_getBestGroupSacrifice(...);

AI_getBestGroupSacrifice's DOMAIN_AIR value does not use iAirCombat either. For these
two default units it rewards interception and divides by production cost. With equal
100% interception and health, the cheaper Fighter receives the higher sacrifice value
(roughly 128*200/140 versus 128*200/170 before common value adjustments), so the
weaker Fighter is selected as the expendable attacker.

This is not what the <68% threshold intends. As a sanity comparison, the pre-LFB
air-aware AI_attackOdds formula on a simple unmodified strength-3 ground defender
would heavily distinguish the units and put both comfortably above the sacrifice
threshold (approximately 97% for air strength 12 and 99% for air strength 24 under
that legacy heuristic). The LFB path instead erases the air-strength distinction and
forces the sacrifice mode through its bogus near-minimum odds.

The same selector is used by getAirStrikePlotHelp, so the displayed interception/help
can also be based on the wrong member of a selected multi-air group.

RELATIONSHIP TO F209 / KI#532
-----------------------------
F209 is a SAS practical-5286 regression: the new low-power ordering feeds aircraft
into AI_currEffectiveStr and asserts because ordinary combat strength is zero.
F210 is older and independent: the inherited LFB selection/odds machinery also uses
ordinary strength where DOMAIN_AIR requires air strength.

The interaction is important for implementation review. Merely fixing F209 by making
bUseLowPower false for DOMAIN_AIR causes the real air attack loop to fall back to the
inherited LFB path, where F210 remains. Therefore F209's repair is necessary but does
not make aircraft selection/odds correct by itself.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
A robust repair needs an explicitly air-aware path rather than passing aircraft
through ordinary LFB combat strength:

1. CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds should not call generic land-combat calculateCombatOdds for
   DOMAIN_AIR. It should use an air-aware estimate (the existing legacy air branch is
   the obvious baseline, though its heuristic can be reviewed separately).
2. CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_getBestGroupAttacker should not call
   LFBgetBetterAttacker for DOMAIN_AIR unless LFB itself is taught to use air combat
   strength. Once AI_attackOdds is air-correct, selecting air candidates by that value
   (with the existing human/sacrifice policy layered afterward) is safer than invoking
   an LFB routine whose attacker-rank contract assumes ordinary combat strength.

Do not "fix" this by giving aircraft fake ordinary iCombat values; the engine
intentionally separates ordinary and air combat strength and many other callers rely
on that distinction.

F207 / KI#530 STRENGTHENING -- "ATTACKER" CENSUS ALSO COUNTS UNITS THAT CANNOT
ACT THIS TURN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) caller/predicate pass strengthened
F207's root again. The human easy-city-capture precheck scans every unit on the plot
and counts a unit when:

    !pUnit->canBombard(kAt) &&
    pUnit->canMoveOrAttackInto(*pMissionPlot)

Earlier proof already established two false-positive classes:
- foreign third-party units can satisfy the ordinary-movement half through Open
  Borders with the target, despite not participating in the human player's war;
- same-owner Spies can satisfy ordinary movement through hostile territory/cities
  while having zero combat strength.

There is a third independent false-positive mode inside the SAME census root:
canMoveOrAttackInto is destination/legal-entry logic and does not test whether the
unit can currently act. CvUnit::canMove() separately rejects exhausted movement,
dead units and immobile-timer units; canMoveInto does not consume that contract.
Therefore a same-owner ordinary combat unit that has already exhausted all movement
can still be counted toward iAttackers and can spuriously flip bEasyCityCapture even
though it cannot take part in the immediate assault this turn.

This reinforces the correct F207 repair boundary. An owner-only filter is necessary
but not sufficient. For the defended-city branch, the census needs to represent
units that the human actually controls AND that can currently act AND that can
actually perform the hostile attack/assault against the target. Generic
canMoveOrAttackInto is too broad because its ordinary-movement half and its lack of a
current-movement check answer a different question.

Do NOT allocate a new root for this symptom; it is further proof of F207's existing
"destination entry used as immediate assault capability" defect.


F208 / KI#531 BOUNDARY CHECK -- INVISIBLE DEFENDER LEAK IS DORMANT IN CURRENT SAS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The same human smart-bombard defender census uses:

    pMissionPlot->plotCount(PUF_canDefendEnemy, getOwner(), false)

where PUF_canDefendEnemy combines canDefend + enemy semantics but does not apply
PUF_isVisible. CvPlot::getNumVisibleEnemyDefenders, by contrast, explicitly adds a
visibility predicate. Thus the local census would count an invisible combat-capable
defender if current game data allowed one to defend the target land city.

Current SAS XML was enumerated rather than assuming such a unit exists. Among 131
UnitInfo entries, the only unit with a real non-NONE Invisible type is
UNIT_ATTACK_SUBMARINE (INVISIBLE_SUBMARINE), DOMAIN_SEA, iCombat=24. There is no
combat-capable invisible DOMAIN_LAND unit. Spies are special-entry/invisible units
but have zero combat and do not satisfy canDefend. A sea submarine cannot defend a
land city under the domain check.

Therefore this is a future-data/API robustness hazard, NOT a current information-leak
finding and not F211. Keep it as a boundary note beside F208; F208's live current-data
proof remains loaded land combat cargo, which canDefend() counts even though primary
getBestDefender() explicitly rejects isCargo().


F204 / KI#527 BOUNDARY CHECK -- GROUP PATHFINDER DOES NOT ADD A NORMAL AIR CALLER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final caller matrix noticed two textual AI_sumStrength references in
GroupPathFinder and challenged whether F204's explicit DOMAIN_AIR assertion could be
reached during normal air pathfinding.

One reference is inside an old fully commented-out experimental path-validity block.
The live reference is in the MOVE_ATTACK_STACK cost path, which immediately asserts:

    FAssert(kGroup.getDomainType() == DOMAIN_LAND);

MOVE_ATTACK_STACK is itself AI-only there. Thus normal air pathfinding does not feed
an aircraft group into AI_sumStrength. F204 remains the inherited debug combat-help
caller mismatch, not a broader pathfinding defect.

F211 / provisional KI#534 -- inherited planned-war mission census can call
AI_isDeclareWar on a supported empty selection group and fire a false debug assert
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED SOURCE-LEVEL DEBUG-CONTRACT DEFECT; RELEASE BUILD RETURNS SAFELY.
INHERITED ROOT: BtS AI_isDeclareWar null-head assertion + BBAI/K-Mod target-mission
census / group-separation lifecycle; present in K-Mod 1.46 and AdvCiv 1.14.
CURRENT SAS DID NOT INTRODUCE THE ROOT.

LOCAL CONTRACT MISMATCH
-----------------------
Current CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_isDeclareWar begins with:

    FAssert(getHeadUnit() != NULL);

but later deliberately reacquires the head and handles its absence:

    CvUnit const* pHeadUnit = getHeadUnit();
    if (pHeadUnit == NULL)
        return false;

The later guard is not dead release-only paranoia. A selection group can legitimately
remain allocated for a bounded interval after its last unit has left.

SUPPORTED EMPTY-GROUP LIFECYCLE
-------------------------------
The final lifecycle trace established all of the following in current SAS:

1. CvUnit::joinGroup removes a unit from its old group through removeUnit(). It does
   not kill the old selection group when that removal empties it.

2. CvSelectionGroup::removeUnit -> deleteUnitNode clears the mission command queue,
   but clearMissionQueue() does NOT clear the AI mission metadata
   (m_eMissionAIType / m_iMissionAIX / m_iMissionAIY / m_missionAIUnit).
   Therefore an emptied group can retain the MissionAI plot that it had while live.

3. If removing a non-human group's head exposes a new head with a different UnitAI,
   CvUnit::joinGroup marks the old group AI_isForceSeparate().

4. CvPlayerAI::AI_unitUpdate has an explicit prepass over the group cycle which calls
   AI_separate() on force-separated groups. AI_separate() rejoins every remaining
   unit into a fresh group. The old group can consequently become empty while staying
   registered in the player's selection-group/group-cycle containers.

5. This is an expected enough state that K-Mod's movement-priority path explicitly
   handles a null head by returning MAX_INT, while CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update
   returns false immediately when getNumUnits() == 0. Neither path destroys the
   object at that point.

6. Destruction is deferred to CvSelectionGroup::doDelayedDeath(). In particular,
   CvPlayer::doTurnUnits starts by iterating all groups and calling doDelayedDeath(),
   which kills groups whose unit count is now zero.

The empty group is therefore a supported transient object, not merely an impossible
state after memory corruption.

LIVE PRE-WAR CALL PATH
----------------------
The first direct-caller pass almost rejected the candidate because the two obvious
current AI_enemyTargetMissions calls are war-only:

- CvTeamAI::AI_endWarVal asserts isAtWar(eTeam);
- the AI_surrenderTrade use occurs in its bWar/capitulation branch.

For both, AI_enemyTargetMissions short-circuits at:

    ::atWar(getTeam(), pMissionPlot->getTeam()) ||
        pLoopSelectionGroup->AI_isDeclareWar(*pMissionPlot)

so AI_isDeclareWar is not evaluated for an already-active war.

However AdvCiv's optimized boolean wrapper AI_isAnyEnemyTargetMission() is also live.
Its important caller is CvTeamAI::AI_abandonWarPlanIfTimedOut, which is invoked for
WARPLAN_LIMITED / WARPLAN_DOGPILE / WARPLAN_TOTAL targets specifically while the team
is NOT yet at war. It asks whether any member has an active mission toward eTarget so
that a still-active invasion plan is not abandoned.

For such a target, ::atWar is false. If an empty group's retained MissionAI plot is
owned by eTarget, AI_enemyTargetMissions therefore evaluates AI_isDeclareWar on that
empty group and trips the leading debug assertion. The later null-head guard would
otherwise return false, and the zero-unit group cannot contribute a positive mission
count.

TURN ORDER MAKES THE WINDOW REAL
--------------------------------
The final ordering proof removes the remaining lifetime ambiguity:

- K-Mod/AdvCiv player activation calls CvTeam::doTurn for the team's leader BEFORE
  that player's doTurnUnits.
- CvTeam::doTurn -> AI_doTurnPost -> AI_doWar.
- AI_doWar can reach AI_abandonWarPlanIfTimedOut and therefore
  AI_isAnyEnemyTargetMission / AI_enemyTargetMissions for a planned, not-yet-declared
  target.
- only AFTER CvTeam::doTurn returns does player activation call CvPlayer::doTurnUnits,
  whose opening doDelayedDeath pass deletes empty groups.

Thus a force-separated group emptied during the prior movement phase can survive
until the next team's war-planning pass and be observed before the normal empty-group
cleanup.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already has the apparently contradictory AI_isDeclareWar shape: a leading
FAssert(getHeadUnit() != NULL), followed later by a null-safe head check. It does not
have BBAI's AI_enemyTargetMissions function.

K-Mod 1.46 imports BBAI's AI_enemyTargetMissions and uses it directly in the pre-war
WARPLAN_LIMITED/DOGPILE and WARPLAN_TOTAL timeout branches while !isAtWar(target).
K-Mod also has the team-doTurn-before-player-doTurnUnits ordering and the deferred
empty-group doDelayedDeath cleanup. Therefore the bad interaction is already present
in K-Mod, not introduced by AdvCiv's later bool wrapper.

AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same underlying census and lifecycle; its
AI_isAnyEnemyTargetMission optimization only changes the maximum count requested.
Current SAS inherits the same contract mismatch.

CONSEQUENCE / SEVERITY
----------------------
This is a debug-build false assertion, not demonstrated release gameplay corruption.
In release builds AI_isDeclareWar reaches its null check and returns false. The empty
group has zero units/cargo, so it cannot increase the mission count either.

The practical cost is nevertheless real for source debugging: a valid transient group
state can stop an assert-enabled run inside normal AI war-plan maintenance. Given this
audit's repeated use of debug assertions to catch genuine state corruption, preserving
assert signal quality is worthwhile.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The narrowest semantically exact repair is in CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions:
ignore empty groups before reading their stale MissionAI target or consulting
AI_isDeclareWar, e.g. alongside the skip-group check:

    if (pLoopSelectionGroup == pSkipSelectionGroup ||
        pLoopSelectionGroup->getNumUnits() <= 0)
    {
        continue;
    }

That is behavior-neutral for valid live counts because a zero-unit group cannot add
units or cargo, and it prevents obsolete AI mission metadata from entering the war
intent classifier.

A broader alternative is to make AI_isDeclareWar's existing null-head release guard
precede or replace the assertion. The caller-side filter is preferable as the first
repair because AI_enemyTargetMissions is a census of actual units and has no reason to
inspect an empty group's stale target at all.

STATUS: CONFIRMED as F211 / provisional KI#534.


WEIGHTED-ODDS FOLLOW-UP -- SUSPECTED DOUBLE ADJUSTMENT REJECTED
---------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP16-era final matrix had one independent-looking concern in
AI_getWeightedOdds(): it subtracts GET_PLAYER(...).AI_getAttackOddsChange() from the
selected group attack odds. That would be wrong if Lead From Behind's alternate
attacker selector returned raw odds without first adding the leader's optimism bonus.

The exact LFB path closes the concern. CvUnitAI::LFBgetBetterAttacker converts its
combat odds to AI odds and then explicitly executes:

    iAIOdds += GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_getAttackOddsChange();

before clamping and returning iAIAttackOdds. Therefore AI_getWeightedOdds removes an
adjustment that really is present. No independent root is created; F200's already
classified clamp/weight issue remains the relevant weighted-odds finding.

F212 is NOT spent here.


FINITE LOW-MENTION PUBLIC-HELPER PASS -- NO NEW ROOT SO FAR
-----------------------------------------------------------
The function-name coverage matrix identified several public helpers with little or no
literal-name discussion in the album. Their current definitions and all current-tree
callers were enumerated rather than assuming that low textual coverage meant low risk.

AI_init / AI_uninit
-------------------
AI_init delegates to AI_reset; AI_uninit is empty; AI_reset clears all mission-AI,
force-separate and queued-group-attack state. Constructor/destructor use the same
lifecycle. No allocation/resource ownership is hidden here and no independent defect
was found.

AI_isHasPathToAreaEnemyCity / AI_isHasPathToAreaPlayerCity
-----------------------------------------------------------
Current live uses are in CvUnitAI city-assault/stranded handling. The player-specific
helper explicitly returns false for getNumUnits() <= 0 before dereferencing area(), so
it already contains the exact empty-group guard missing from F211's mission census.
For live groups it restricts candidate cities to the group's area, calls generatePath
with the requested movement flags and max-turn bound, and rechecks iPathTurns when a
bound is supplied.

The enemy wrapper applies bMajorOnly as documented and requires
GET_TEAM(getTeam()).AI_mayAttack(candidate team) before testing pathability. Current
callers invoke it through a live CvUnitAI group. No null-group, wrong-team or max-turn
contract defect survived this pass.

AI_isStranded
-------------
This K-Mod helper is intentionally a mission-state query:

    AI_getMissionAIType() == MISSIONAI_STRANDED

The current callers use that marker to order movement priority, preserve stranded
state in unit behavior/help, and let transports discover groups advertised for pickup.
The actual determination / coast-routing work is in CvUnitAI::AI_handleStranded; the
helper is not pretending to recompute geographical strandedness. No defect found in
this accessor contract.

AI_getHeadUnit
--------------
Both AdvCiv const/non-const wrappers read headUnitNode and return NULL when no node
exists. All current external callers were enumerated. The direct dereference in
CvUnitAI's transport-load remainder path is preceded by:

    pRemainderGroup == NULL || pRemainderGroup->getNumUnits() <= 0

so a head must exist under the normal group invariant. Other callers either test NULL
or use a group already anchored by a live acting unit. The new SAS game-record caller
also explicitly null-checks the group before asking for the head.

No new F212 root emerged from these low-mention helpers.

FINDING-LEDGER CORRECTION -- F198 AND F205 WERE ACCIDENTALLY DOUBLE-PROMOTED
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Comparing the frozen finding texts side by side exposed a bookkeeping error in C018:

    F198/KI#521 promoted the false human undefended-city Bombard assertion.
    F205/KI#528 later promoted the very same assertion again.

WIP08 then explicitly said that F205's deeper release-build consequence was the
"same root" and that "no new F-number is consumed," even though F205 had already been
assigned. That is internally inconsistent and should not be carried into closure.

There is, however, a real *second faulty behavior* in the same supported
undefended-city state, and it survives the KI#521 assertion repair:

    scaled rOdds = per100(pUnit->AI_attackOdds(pMissionPlot, false));
    rPriority *= (1 - rOdds);

With no defender, CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds returns 100. Therefore rOdds == 1 and every
eligible Bombarder's otherwise meaningful human ordering priority is multiplied by
zero. All candidates tie at zero and AI_bestUnitForMission falls back to group/unit
iteration order. This is distinct from the now-fixed false assertion: deleting the
assertion does not repair the release ordering collapse.

Least-destructive ledger repair for the cumulative album:

- F198 / KI#521 remains exactly the false debug assertion root and is now FIXED in
  the supplied 13:41 source.
- F205 is RETRACTED AS A DUPLICATE ASSERTION PROMOTION and RE-SCOPED, without changing

F205 / PROVISIONAL KI#528 -- RE-SCOPED RELEASE ORDERING ROOT CONFIRMED
---------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP18 intentionally left one final challenge open: after retiring F205's accidental
duplicate promotion of the KI#521 assertion, is the remaining undefended-city
Bombard priority collapse actually capable of changing supported gameplay, or is it
merely a meaningless tie?

It is gameplay-relevant.

Current AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) builds a meaningful per-unit priority
from human intent, bombard damage, wasted bombard damage and other factors, then does:

    scaled rOdds = per100(pUnit->AI_attackOdds(pMissionPlot, false));
    rPriority *= (1 - rOdds);

CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds returns 100 when the plot has no defender. Therefore, on a
legal human Bombard command against an undefended city, every otherwise-differentiated
candidate receives a final priority of zero. Because replacement requires
`rPriority > rMaxPriority`, the selector keeps the first eligible unit in group-list
order instead of the unit selected by the intended Bombard priority model.

The decisive supported state is the human zero-current-defense maintenance Bombard:

- CvCity::isBombardable deliberately allows a human Bombard at current defense 0 when
  total defense is still positive and the city has not yet been bombarded this turn.
- This is meaningful, not UI residue: CvCity::changeDefenseModifier marks the city as
  bombarded even when the effective defense change is zero, suppressing defense
  recovery for that turn.
- CvSelectionGroup::startMission repeatedly selects a Bombard unit and calls
  CvUnit::bombard.
- The first selected unit pays its attack/movement cost; the city becomes bombarded.
- The city's special zero-defense human isBombardable allowance then becomes false,
  so the group mission terminates after that one unit.

Thus the collapsed selector decides which single siege/bombard unit pays the action
cost. Group-list order is not Bombard intent; a stronger or more valuable unit can be
spent while a more appropriate unit remains unused. The effect is deterministic for
a given group ordering, not merely cosmetic.

Ancestry makes the root unusually clear. AdvCiv practical commit 2809,
"Smarter code for order of group bombardment", introduced the modern richer priority
calculation and the attack-odds multiplier. Before that change the undefended state
still retained differentiation based on actual/wasted bombard and unit preservation.
The multiplier therefore regressed precisely the ordering that the commit was trying
to improve. Later AdvCiv changes alter individual factors but leave this root intact.

Ledger boundary after reconciliation:

- F198/KI#521 = false debug assertion for legal undefended human Bombard; fixed in the
  supplied 13:41 source.
- F205/provisional KI#528 = independent release-build ordering collapse caused by
  multiplying the Bombard priority by zero when AI_attackOdds returns 100 for an
  undefended target; still present in the supplied source.

The clean repair boundary is to avoid using ordinary attack odds as a zeroing factor
when there is no defender. Exact implementation should be reviewed with the intended
human Bombard ordering semantics; deleting or special-casing the no-defender factor is
safer than reviving the old assertion.

HISTORICAL REOPEN -- K-MOD 271 PRESERVED
-----------------------------------------
K-Mod practical 271, "Fixed a rare infinite-loop bug, indirectly caused by the K-Mod
change in groupAttack", was reopened because its commit number had not been explicitly
classified in the durable tail despite the current behavior having been inspected.

Its CvSelectionGroupAI fix changed the AI_update head check from merely testing
`isDelayedDeath()` to actively executing `doDelayedDeath()` before continuing. Current
SAS preserves that behavior:

    CvUnitAI* pHeadUnit = AI_getHeadUnit();
    if (pHeadUnit == NULL || pHeadUnit->doDelayedDeath())
        break;

The companion group-timer change that updates all queued combats rather than breaking
after the first fighting unit is also preserved in current CvSelectionGroup. No
partial reversion or new root was found. Rejected as F212.

F212 / PROVISIONAL KI#535 -- K-MOD 846 REINTRODUCED A K-MOD 428 AMPHIBIOUS
GROUP-ATTACK CANCELLATION WINDOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS: CONFIRMED inherited K-Mod regression; present in final K-Mod 1.46, AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS.

ROOT
----
A turn-start `isForceUpdate()` flag can survive on a land cargo group until after its
transport has already ordered that cargo group to begin an immediate amphibious
attack. The first attack queues K-Mod's deferred group-attack continuation, but the
cargo group's later AI_update sees the *old* force-update flag and cancels the *new*
queued attack before executing it.

This is exactly the class of failure K-Mod practical 428 explicitly fixed, but K-Mod
practical 846 later reshaped force-update semantics in a way that reopened it.

CURRENT-RUNTIME PROOF
---------------------
1. CvSelectionGroup::doTurn is run for AI land groups at turn activation, including
   loaded cargo groups. In current source there is exactly one live producer of
   `setForceUpdate(true)`: this turn-start path.

   For an AI-controlled group whose activity is not ACTIVITY_MISSION, doTurn does:

       setForceUpdate(true);
       clearMissionQueue();
       AI().AI_cancelGroupAttack();

   Therefore any pre-existing queued group attack is already canceled here. The force
   flag that remains is only a request that the group receive at least one AI update.

2. The loaded sea transport normally moves before its land cargo group. Current
   CvPlayerAI::AI_movementPriority gives a non-special loaded sea transport priority
   3, whereas ordinary land combat cargo is much later (bombard/collateral around
   11/12, ordinary fighting groups roughly around the 65-based land scale). This is
   the exact ordering anticipated by K-Mod's surviving comment:

       "this is required for amphibious assaults; during which a low priority group
        can be ordered to attack before its turn."

3. When the transport reaches an adjacent amphibious target,
   CvSelectionGroup::groupAmphibMove obtains the cargo groups and pushes
   MISSION_MOVE_TO directly onto each eligible cargo group.

4. CvSelectionGroup::pushMission starts AI commands immediately:

       insertAtEndMissionQueue(mission, !bAppend || isAIControlled());

   The cargo group's own AI_update has therefore not run yet and its turn-start
   force-update flag is still true, but the transport can already make the cargo
   attack.

5. The MISSION_MOVE_TO execution reaches groupAttack against the adjacent defended
   target. For ordinary AI combat, stack-attack player option handling is false, so
   groupAttack issues one attack and, when multiple units remain and
   MOVE_SINGLE_ATTACK is not set, records the continuation through:

       AI().AI_queueGroupAttack(targetX, targetY);

   AI_queueGroupAttack only sets m_bGroupAttack and its target coordinates. It does
   not clear m_bForceUpdate.

6. Combat resolution clears the ordinary mission queue. The queued group-attack
   state is therefore the dedicated mechanism that tells the AI to continue the
   multi-unit assault after the first combat.

7. AI_movementPriority gives a group with AI_isGroupAttack() priority -1, explicitly
   so this deferred amphibious continuation can run promptly. Whether combat resolved
   synchronously or the global update waits for the combat to stop, the cargo group
   eventually reaches its own CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update with:

       isForceUpdate() == true
       AI_isGroupAttack() == true

8. Current AI_update begins with:

       if (isForceUpdate())
           AI_cancelGroupAttack();

   It therefore deletes the freshly queued amphibious continuation before reaching
   the loop whose first condition is supposed to execute it:

       while ((AI_isGroupAttack() && !isBusy()) || readyToMove())

   The remaining cargo units do not receive the intended forced follow-through from
   that queued state. The turn-start signal has incorrectly overridden newer combat
   state created later in the same movement phase.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SPECULATIVE ORDERING
--------------------------------------
The current priority model strongly favors the loaded sea transport over normal land
cargo, so the transport-before-cargo sequence is ordinary behavior rather than a rare
scheduler coincidence. K-Mod practical 428 itself documents the same requirement:
a low-priority cargo group can be ordered to attack before its own turn, hence a
queued group attack must receive top movement priority afterward.

ANCESTRY -- K-MOD 428 -> K-MOD 846 REGRESSION
---------------------------------------------
K-Mod practical 428 / commit 85a83db596 is titled:

    "Fixed three bugs from the original BtS code which could sometimes cause the
     AI's amphibious group-attacks to be canceled prematurely."

Among its fixes:

- AI_movementPriority began returning -1 for AI_isGroupAttack(), specifically for
  amphibious assaults whose cargo may be ordered to attack before its turn.
- CvSelectionGroup::doTurn stopped leaving a deferred force-update flag and instead
  called doForceUpdate immediately. The source comment says this prevents the forced
  update from interrupting amphibious assaults.
- AI_update's force-update handling was centralized through that immediate cleanup.

K-Mod practical 846 / commit 5348a1d503 later intentionally changed the model:

- turn start once again does `setForceUpdate(true)` and performs mission/group-attack
  cleanup explicitly;
- readyToMove treats force update as sufficient to enter AI processing;
- doForceUpdate is disabled;
- AI_update cancels a group attack when it sees isForceUpdate, without first clearing
  the flag;
- the flag is cleared only after entering the AI_update loop, or in the end cleanup
  path when the group cannot enter the loop.

The full 846 commit message says force update should now merely signal that every AI
group's update function runs at least once per turn, and that AI_cancelGroupAttack and
clearMissionQueue are called explicitly rather than being directly associated with
force update. Yet the new AI_update entry retained exactly such an association:
`isForceUpdate() -> AI_cancelGroupAttack()`.

No later K-Mod change repairs this interaction. Final K-Mod 1.46 retains the same
turn-start flag, immediate amphibious cargo command, queued group-attack priority and
AI_update-entry cancellation. AdvCiv and current SAS inherit that lineage.

SCOPE / CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
The root applies when a transport orders a multi-unit cargo group into an amphibious
attack before that cargo group's own turn/update and the first combat leaves a queued
follow-through to the same target. Instead of continuing the stack attack as K-Mod's
queue mechanism intends, the stale turn-start force-update marker can cancel it.

Practical consequence: an AI naval invasion can spend only the first attack from a
cargo group at that stage instead of following through with the remaining attackers,
weakening or delaying amphibious assaults. Exact visible severity depends on combat
resolution, remaining defenders/attackers and later AI opportunities, but the state
transition itself is deterministic once the above conditions hold.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The strongest narrow observation is that current source has only one live
`setForceUpdate(true)` producer, and that producer already explicitly cancels any
pre-existing group attack at turn start. Therefore the extra AI_update-entry
cancellation is redundant for old turn-start group-attack state but destructive for a
new group attack queued later in the movement phase.

A natural repair candidate is consequently to remove the AI_update-entry
`AI_cancelGroupAttack()` association with isForceUpdate, letting the loop consume a
fresh AI_isGroupAttack state. Because the loop clears forceUpdate before executing
its first action, the end-of-function force-update cleanup then does not cancel that
fresh attack. This also matches K-Mod 846's stated conceptual contract that force
update is merely an update-request signal rather than group-attack cleanup.

An alternative local repair would be to clear the stale force-update flag when
AI_queueGroupAttack records a newer continuation. That is more local but couples the
queue setter to turn-update state; review against the external wrapper and any future
force-update producers would be prudent. Do not patch blindly; the root proof is
stronger than any particular implementation recommendation.

Historical classification:

    introduced fix lineage: K-Mod practical 428 / 85a83db596
    regression lineage:     K-Mod practical 846 / 5348a1d503
    present in:              final K-Mod 1.46, AdvCiv 1.14, current SAS
    SAS-specific:            no

  handling already audited.

  half survives, but the force-update half was later undermined by K-Mod 846, yielding
  F212.
- K-Mod 449 disabled compare-ratio experiment: no live behavior.
- K-Mod 466 const-only MissionAI accessor change: no behavior.

F212 / PROVISIONAL KI#535 -- FINAL RE-CHALLENGE AND REPAIR-BOUNDARY REFINEMENT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
F212 remains CONFIRMED. The re-challenge strengthened the state-contract proof and
found a second place where the same stale turn-start force-update marker can outrank a
newer queued group attack.

Current CvPlayerAI::AI_unitUpdate performs this force-separation pre-pass before
building its movement-priority list:

    if (pLoopSelectionGroup->AI_isForceSeparate())
    {
        if (pLoopSelectionGroup->isForceUpdate() ||
            !pLoopSelectionGroup->AI_isGroupAttack())
        {
            pLoopSelectionGroup->AI_separate();
        }
    }

Thus the stale force-update state can defeat fresh group-attack state in TWO places:

1. If AI_isForceSeparate() becomes true after the initial pre-pass -- e.g. combat
   removes a group head and exposes a different UnitAI -- the next AI_unitUpdate
   pre-pass can split the group despite its newly queued attack because the stale
   isForceUpdate() makes the condition true.

2. If the group survives that pre-pass, CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update still begins by
   canceling AI_isGroupAttack() whenever isForceUpdate() is true.

The state provenance is unusually strong. A complete current-tree grep finds only one
live setForceUpdate(true) producer:

    CvSelectionGroup::doTurn

That turn-start producer already calls clearMissionQueue() and AI_cancelGroupAttack().
Therefore a later state satisfying both:

    isForceUpdate() == true
    AI_isGroupAttack() == true

contains group-attack state that was created AFTER the old turn-start cleanup. The
queued attack is newer information than the force-update marker.

The current tree likewise has only the ordinary groupAttack gameplay producer of
AI_queueGroupAttack, plus the preserved external ABI wrapper. groupAttack queues the
continuation after the first attack when multiple attackers remain and the attack is
not a single-attack command.

The movement scheduler reinforces rather than weakens the amphibious proof. Loaded
sea transports have very high movement priority and can issue immediate cargo missions
before ordinary land cargo receives its own AI_update. If combat makes the game busy,
the next AI_unitUpdate rebuilds priorities; AI_isGroupAttack then gives the cargo group
priority -1, but the force-separation pre-pass runs before sorting and the AI_update
entry cancellation remains afterward. The queued continuation is therefore exposed to
both stale-force-update consumers.

K-Mod 428 explicitly introduced the top-priority queued attack and immediate
force-update handling to prevent premature amphibious cancellation. K-Mod 846 later
states that force update should merely ensure each AI group receives an update at
least once and that AI_cancelGroupAttack / clearMissionQueue are now called explicitly
"without being directly associated with force update." Its new AI_update entry
nonetheless retained exactly such a direct association. Final K-Mod 1.46, AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS retain it.

REPAIR BOUNDARY REFINED
-----------------------
The WIP19 suggestion to remove only the AI_update-entry AI_cancelGroupAttack is not
sufficient, because the AI_unitUpdate force-separation pre-pass can still destroy the
fresh attack.

Two repair families deserve review:

A. Make both consumers respect newer queued attack state -- i.e. do not let a stale
   force-update marker override AI_isGroupAttack in either the force-separation
   pre-pass or AI_update entry.

B. Clear the stale force-update marker when AI_queueGroupAttack records a newer attack
   continuation.

B is compact and naturally orders the two pieces of state, but should not be applied
blindly. CvUnitAI::AI_evacuateCity uses !isForceUpdate() as a proxy for whether a group
has already received its normal AI update this turn; clearing the bit early can change
that heuristic before AI_update has actually executed. A is therefore semantically
more conservative unless caller review proves B harmless.

The root is stronger than any particular patch recommendation. Keep F212 scoped to the
stale-force-update/newer-group-attack ordering contract and review both cancellation
sites together.

- AI_isDeclareWarExternal preserves the original nullable plot contract by returning
  false for NULL before calling the newer reference-based internal implementation.
- AI_attackOddsExternal, AI_getBestGroupAttackerExternal and
  AI_ejectBestDefenderExternal still require the same non-null plot arguments as their
  original interfaces; adding speculative null semantics is not justified.
- compare/sum-strength legacy arguments intentionally remain compatibility shims around
  the K-Mod-reduced internal APIs.
- No virtual slot/signature drift or newly reachable low-power behavior was found.

Rejected as F213.

AI_getBombardTurns GLOBAL-BOMBER APPROXIMATION -- REJECTED AS DEFECT
--------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_getBombardTurns grants a synthetic air contribution whenever the owner has any air
bombard unit globally. A bomber elsewhere on the map can therefore shorten an unrelated
land group's projected bombard horizon and make building defense look ignorable.

This is coarse, but the complete caller/ancestry check does not support classifying it
as a correctness defect:

- the helper explicitly documents an approximate number of bombard turns;
- even a group with zero real bombard capability receives a finite estimate rather
  than an "impossible" sentinel;
- callers use the result as a strategic heuristic/value modifier, not as a legality or
  reachability guarantee;
- the global bHasBomber term is deliberate BBAI/K-Mod ancestry rather than an accidental
  SAS mutation.

Record as an intentional coarse strategic approximation / possible tuning weakness,
not F213.

QUEUE-031 INITIAL DELTA CLASSIFICATION
--------------------------------------
A normalized function-body comparison was performed before the inherited audit so that
CRLF/comment/formatting churn in the raw diff would not be mistaken for SAS behavior.
Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 each contain the same 61 UWAICache.cpp function
definitions. Only two function bodies differ behaviorally:

    UWAICache::calculateThreatRating
    UWAICache::updateWarAnger

Both differences are already-owned reviewed repairs rather than new queue-031 roots:

* updateWarAnger is the F112 / KI#435 repair. AdvCiv divided an enemy-team war-weariness
  contribution by the cache owner's team size even though the team contribution is
  consumed once per living enemy player. Current SAS divides by that enemy team's
  living-member count.

* calculateThreatRating is the F121 / KI#444 bounded startup-clock repair. AdvCiv used
  currentEra <= startEra as an unbounded startup guard; a terminal-era start can never
  leave the starting era. Current SAS preserves the era shortcut but bounds it by 25
  normalized startup turns.

The current UWAICache.h normalized diff is formatting-only. No SAS data member or public
cache ABI change was found at queue entry.


F213 / provisional KI#536
-------------------------
TITLE
    Full UWAICache reset does not clear m_readyToCapitulateTo, so a new game or loaded
    save can inherit human-capitulation authorization from an earlier in-memory game.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv/UWAI cache-reset and save-load defect dating to the
    initial 2017 WarAndPeaceAI cache integration; present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
    AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
    m_readyToCapitulateTo is persistent temporal authorization state. It is serialized:

        pStream->Write(m_readyToCapitulateTo.size());
        ...
        pStream->Write(*it);

    and restored by insertion:

        int iSize;
        pStream->Read(&iSize);
        for (int i = 0; i < iSize; i++)
        {
            TeamTypes eMaster;
            pStream->Read((int*)&eMaster);
            ...
            m_readyToCapitulateTo.insert(eMaster);
        }

    read() explicitly calls the cache's full reset first:

        m_eOwner = ...;
        // Important to set owner first b/c clear uses it
        clear();

    However, UWAICache::clear(false) resets/deallocates every neighboring persistent
    team cache family -- past war score, bounty, sponsor, hireability, military branches,
    etc. -- without ever clearing m_readyToCapitulateTo. init() and uninit() also call
    this same full clear(). Therefore the set is neither replacement-read state nor a
    clean new-game state.

SAVE/OBJECT-REUSE PROOF
    This is not dependent on allocator reuse speculation. UWAICache.h documents the
    intended object lifecycle explicitly: CvPlayer objects are reset and reused when
    returning to the opening menu or loading a savegame; read() is supposed to reset
    the cache data members, while init() resets them for a new game. CvPlayerAI allocates
    m_pUWAI once in its constructor and deletes it only in the CvPlayerAI destructor.
    UWAI::Player::init/read simply delegate into the existing m_cache object.

    Consequently a supported sequence is:

    1. In game A, AI player P's leader cache obtains ReadyToCapitulate(H)=true for human
       team H.
    2. Return to menu and start game B, or load save B in the same Civ4 process.
    3. The existing P cache is reset/reused. init() or read() calls clear(false), but
       the old H entry survives.
    4. For a loaded save whose serialized ready set does NOT contain H, read() inserts
       only the save's actual entries but never erases the stale H entry. The resulting
       state is effectively OLD_SET union SAVED_SET instead of SAVED_SET.

    Thus the exact same save can yield a different m_readyToCapitulateTo state when
    loaded in a fresh process versus after another game. A new game can likewise begin
    with authorization inherited from the previous game occupying that player slot.

CONSEQUENCE
    CvTeamAI::AI_surrenderTrade deliberately treats this bit as a gate proving that
    UWAI::Team::considerPeace has authorized capitulation to a human master. A stale true
    can therefore satisfy that temporal safeguard even though the current game/save never
    granted it. The ordinary power, war-success, city and diplomacy surrender checks still
    apply; this finding does NOT claim unconditional immediate capitulation. The defect is
    state contamination / save-load nondeterminism in an authorization bit whose explicit
    purpose is to prevent capitulation before the current AI-turn decision path runs.

RELATION TO F196 / KI#519
    F196 is a different lifecycle root: within one continuous game, a valid authorization
    from war A survives ordinary peace and can be reused in later war B because war end
    does not clear it.

    F213 is the stronger full-reset/save-load boundary: even a new game or an unrelated
    loaded save can inherit authorization from an earlier in-memory game because clear()
    itself fails to reset the serialized set. Fixing either root alone does not prove the
    other fixed. They may share the same state variable but violate different lifecycle
    contracts and need separate regression tests.

ANCESTRY
    The initial AdvCiv WarAndPeaceAI integration commit (practical 1253,
    f6ff6a182f, 2017-04-16) introduced the same combination in WarAndPeaceCache:

    * readyToCapitulate is serialized;
    * read() calls clear() and then inserts each loaded master team;
    * init() calls clear();
    * clear(false) resets neighboring persistent data but never clears
      readyToCapitulate.

    Later renaming/refactoring from WarAndPeaceCache to UWAICache preserves the omission.
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS still have it unchanged.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Reset this set only on a FULL cache reset, alongside the state that is intentionally
    not recomputed by update():

        if (!bBeforeUpdate)
        {
            ...
            m_readyToCapitulateTo.clear();
            ...
        }

    Do not blindly clear it in the common portion of clear(), because update() calls
    clear(true) every player/team turn and the readiness authorization is intentionally
    allowed to survive ordinary cache recomputation long enough to serve the human
    capitulation gate. F196 separately argues for clearing the corresponding target on
    war end.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not caused by old save versions. The set has been serialized since the
      initial cache implementation, and current version-9 reads have the same union
      behavior.
    * std::set suppresses duplicate entries, so the bug is not duplicate growth; it is
      retention of stale team IDs absent from the incoming save/new game.
    * The neighboring m_bOffensiveTrait / m_bDefensiveTrait fields are not analogous:
      init() immediately recomputes them and read() overwrites them from the stream.
    * clear(true) intentionally preserves several asynchronously maintained fields;
      the defect is specifically that clear(false), whose documented purpose is a full
      reset for init/read/uninit, also preserves this serialized authorization set.


OTHER QUEUE-ENTRY WORK / NEGATIVE CONTROLS
------------------------------------------
* createMilitaryBranches/deleteMilitaryBranches and city-list ownership were traced
  through init, read, uninit and the destructor. read() calls clear(false), which deletes
  the old military branch objects before createMilitaryBranches; no duplicate-vector
  allocation root was found there.
* m_abPlayerLocated exists in the header but has no live references in current SAS or
  Base AdvCiv 1.14. Its lack of reset/serialization is dead state, not a gameplay cache
  defect.
* m_aiReachableCities' own-player value is initialized from getNumCities in clear(),
  while incremental City::add only adjusts foreign owners. Current consumers query
  foreign/target players rather than relying on the cache owner's own slot, so no live
  incremental own-city count defect has been promoted.

F214 / provisional KI#537
-------------------------
TITLE
    MilitaryBranch typical-unit refresh is sticky: when a branch loses every currently
    trainable candidate, the cache keeps its old unit and can forecast military capacity
    that no longer exists (current concrete case: losing Uranium retains nuclear buildup).

STATUS
    CONFIRMED CURRENT CROSS-FILE CACHE-REFRESH DEFECT. Root is inherited from the initial
    2017 UWAI/MilitaryBranch integration and is unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
    AdvCiv-SAS. Reached from queue 031 through UWAICache::updateTypicalUnits; the local
    implementation lives in queue 064 MilitaryBranch.cpp and must be treated as an
    already-owned root when that file is audited later.

ROOT
    UWAICache::update() calls updateTypicalUnits() every ordinary cache refresh:

        updateTypicalUnits();

    and UWAICache::updateTypicalUnits() asks every persistent MilitaryBranch object to
    refresh itself:

        for (size_t i = 0; i < m_militaryPower.size(); i++)
            m_militaryPower[i]->updateTypicalUnit();

    However, MilitaryBranch::updateTypicalUnit() does not invalidate m_eTypicalUnit or
    m_rTypicalPower before looking for the best CURRENTLY trainable candidate. It merely
    overwrites them when a candidate beats the default-zero rBestValue. If no candidate
    survives the trainability/domain/utility checks, the previous turn's unit and power
    remain cached.

    NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit() independently repeats the same pattern rather
    than calling the base implementation. It even returns immediately when the owner has
    no capital without clearing the old nuke first.

    Therefore these functions implement "replace if a new candidate exists" rather than
    the required refresh/replacement semantics "compute the best current candidate, or
    NO_UNIT if there is none."

CURRENT-SAS NUCLEAR REPRODUCTION
    This is live under the supplied current XML, not merely a future-mod robustness case.
    Both current nuclear units require Uranium:

        UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE  -> BonusType BONUS_URANIUM
        UNIT_ICBM           -> BonusType BONUS_URANIUM

    and both require Fission + Rocketry. CvCity::canTrain delegates to CvPlot::canTrain;
    with bTestVisible=false, CvPlot::canTrain explicitly rejects a unit whose required
    BonusType is not connected/available in that city.

    Supported sequence:

    1. Player P has Fission/Rocketry and Uranium. Its capital can train an ICBM or
       Tactical Nuke. UWAICache::update -> NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit stores a
       nuclear m_eTypicalUnit and matching m_rTypicalPower.
    2. P then loses its last connected Uranium (e.g. improvement/resource connection is
       lost or the supplying trade ends) while remaining otherwise alive and developed.
    3. On the next cache update, the Nuclear branch scans the same civ units. The capital
       canTrain checks now reject both nukes.
    4. No candidate enters the rLoopValue > rBestValue assignment, but the routine never
       first sets m_eTypicalUnit=NO_UNIT. The old nuke therefore survives indefinitely
       while Uranium remains unavailable.

    This is a post-refresh stale value, not merely the expected one-turn interval between
    an asynchronous resource change and the next UWAICache update.

DIRECT WAR-EVALUATION CONSEQUENCE
    InvasionGraph::Node::initMilitary() copies the current cached MilitaryBranch objects,
    including the stale NuclearArsenal, into the simulation.

    ArmamentForecast then deliberately reserves an offensive nuclear buildup share
    (20 percent in current AdvCiv/SAS) and documents the intended safeguard:

        // Undone below if unable to build nukes

    The safeguard is exactly the typical-unit test shared by all branches:

        if (m_kMilitary[i]->getTypicalUnit() == NO_UNIT)
        {
            rSurplus += rBranchPortions[i];
            rBranchPortions[i] = 0;
        }

    Because the stale Nuclear branch still reports the old nuke, the safeguard does not
    fire. The forecast later calls getTypicalCost/getTypicalPower and converts the
    nuclear branch's production share into predicted extra nuclear military power even
    though no city can currently train a nuke.

    This can feed InvasionGraph/MilitaryAnalyst/WarEvaluator with an overstated armament
    trajectory and therefore alter war/peace utility decisions. It does not require the
    player to have zero existing nukes; the defect is specifically that FUTURE production
    is forecast from a unit that is no longer trainable.

BROADER SAME-ROOT MANIFESTATIONS
    The stale-refresh contract is not nuclear-specific.

    * For sea branches the base update uses CvTeamAI::AI_isExpectingToTrain, which scans
      actual cities and requires a qualifying coastal city that can train the unit. A civ
      that loses its last useful coastal city can therefore have no current Fleet or
      Logistics candidate while retaining the old cached ship/transport. ArmamentForecast
      can then continue assigning naval production to capacity the civ can no longer
      build, and UWAICache::shipSpeed can continue using a stale Logistics transport.

    * Any branch whose last trainable candidate disappears through a resource/prerequisite
      change has the same sticky-unit behavior. Nuclear is the clearest current-data case
      because both current nuke types share the same removable Uranium requirement.

    These are manifestations of one refresh-invalidation root, not additional finding IDs.

ANCESTRY / INTENT PROOF
    Practical AdvCiv commit 1253 (f6ff6a182f, 2017-04-16), the initial WarAndPeace/UWAI
    cache integration, already contains both sides of the contradiction:

    * MilitaryBranch::updateTypicalUnit and NuclearArsenal::updateTypicalUnit assign the
      stored typical unit only after finding a better candidate and never clear it at
      refresh start.
    * The initial ArmamentForecast comments that its 25-percent nuclear share is
      "Undone below if unable to build nukes" and implements that by testing whether the
      branch's typical unit is NULL.

    Thus the cache value was intended from its introduction to represent CURRENT
    buildability, but the invalidation case was omitted. Later refactors changed names,
    containers and numeric types but preserve the sticky refresh. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current SAS remain behaviorally the same here.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    At minimum, each typical-unit refresh must begin from an invalid/no-candidate state:

        m_eTypicalUnit = NO_UNIT;
        m_rTypicalPower = 0;

    before scanning candidates. This must also be done in NuclearArsenal's independent
    override (or centralized in a helper that every override invokes), and before its
    early no-capital return.

    Do not reset m_rTotalPower or m_iUnits: those are separately maintained counts of the
    military actually possessed, not trainability estimates.

    Fleet has one related derived-cache detail that must not be missed when implementing
    the general repair. Fleet::updateTypicalUnit currently updates m_bCanBombard only if
    getTypicalUnit()!=NO_UNIT. Once the typical unit is correctly invalidated, a no-candidate
    Fleet must also leave m_bCanBombard false rather than retaining the old ship's flag.
    Army::updateCanBombard/updateCanSoften already recompute their booleans to a false
    fallback on every refresh.

    Queue 064 MilitaryBranch.cpp should revisit implementation mechanics and any additional
    derived-field siblings, but must not allocate a new root for this already-proven
    typical-unit invalidation defect.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not a serialization-only issue. A correctly serialized old typical unit
      should be refreshed on the next UWAICache update; the bug is that refresh itself
      cannot express "no candidate now."
    * Existing nuclear power is tracked separately by m_rTotalPower and unit reports.
      Clearing the typical unit does not erase or undercount already-built nukes.
    * The issue does not depend on tech loss, which ordinary Civ4 rarely permits. Current
      SAS Uranium availability can change during normal play while the nuclear techs and
      player remain valid.
    * A branch changing from one trainable unit to another is normally safe because a new
      candidate overwrites the old value. The failing transition is specifically
      SOME_CANDIDATE -> NO_CURRENT_CANDIDATE.


PRESERVED-FIELD MATRIX -- INTERIM NOTES
---------------------------------------
* The earlier onTeamLeaderChanged / m_abCanBeHiredAgainst seam remains under review and is
  NOT F215 at this checkpoint. A newly selected AI team leader can carry its old team's
  hireability bits through a Permanent Alliance because onTeamLeaderChanged does not reset
  that map despite its comment saying CanBeHired should start false. However, the actual
  declareWarTrade path still performs legality/attitude checks and a fresh WarEvaluator
  before accepting a sponsored war. The stale true bit may therefore be chiefly an
  alert/evaluation-suppression timing discrepancy rather than a demonstrated incorrect
  war authorization. Do not promote without a stronger consequence proof.

* F214 is distinct from F213. F213 is a full-reset/read replacement failure in a serialized
  capitulation-authorization set. F214 is an ordinary per-turn refresh failure in a
  trainability-derived military estimate.
